2026-12-06.title: Second Sunday of Annunciation
2026-12-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Balaam receives instructions from the angel
Pray that we may declare the mystery of Christ
The Annunciation of the birth of Christ
2026-12-06.alt: Season of Annunciation. The 25 Days' Fast continues.
2026-12-06.verse: Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
theo: The second Sunday of the season brings us to the heart of the Annunciation: Gabriel is sent to Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to Joseph, of the house of David. “Greetings, favoured one! The Lord is with you.” Mary is troubled, asks how this can be, and receives the answer: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.” Then she says the word on which our salvation turns: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”

The Old Testament reading offers a surprising contrast. Balaam, a foreign seer hired to curse Israel, cannot see the angel of the Lord standing in his path; even his donkey sees more than he does. Only when the Lord opens his eyes does he bow down, and then he says: “The word God puts in my mouth, that is what I must say.” Balaam obeys God's word reluctantly; Mary welcomes it freely. Balaam later prophesies, “A star shall come out of Jacob” (Numbers 24:17); Mary gives birth to that Star.

Isaiah promises that God will blot out transgressions and “pour my spirit upon your descendants.” At Nazareth that promise begins: the Spirit comes upon Mary, and the Word becomes flesh in her womb. Paul asks the Colossians to pray “that God will open to us a door for the word, that we may declare the mystery of Christ.” Mary is the first open door for the Word.
Our Church loves Mary because she shows what every Christian is called to be: a listener who becomes a bearer of Christ. In this season, her “yes” is the model for ours.
conn: The donkey and the Virgin.
The Fathers noticed the contrast: Balaam's donkey saw the angel when the prophet did not; the humble Virgin received the angel when the learned did not. God reveals himself to the lowly (Luke 10:21).
A star from Jacob.
Balaam's later oracle (Numbers 24:17) was read by Jews and Christians as messianic. The Magi followed a star to the child born of Mary (Matthew 2:2).
The throne of David.
Gabriel's promise (Luke 1:32–33) fulfils Nathan's oracle to David: “I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever” (2 Samuel 7:13).
Overshadowing.
“Overshadow” (Luke 1:35) is used of the cloud covering the tent of meeting when God's glory filled it (Exodus 40:35). Mary becomes the new dwelling of God.
altar: At the epiclesis of the Qurbana the priest asks the Holy Spirit to come upon the offerings. The same Spirit who overshadowed Mary makes Christ present on the altar. Like Mary, we receive the Word made flesh, and like her we are sent to carry him.
outline: Ask: what one word could change your life? Mary's word “yes” changed the world.
Balaam could not see the angel; God opened his eyes. Ask God to open yours this Advent season.
Point 2 · The Spirit will come upon you
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled in Mary: the Spirit makes her the dwelling of the Son of God.
Point 3 · Here am I, the servant of the Lord
Mary's free yes is the model of faith. What is God asking you to say yes to?
The small house of Nazareth: an ordinary home where heaven's greatest event happened.
“Let it be with me according to your word.”
live: Pray the Angelus at noon every day until Christmas.
Open a door for the Word (Colossians 4:3)
Speak of Christ to one person this week.
Say yes today to one thing you know God is asking of you.
fathers: St Bernard of Clairvaux
“The angel awaits your answer… The whole world is waiting, prostrate at your feet. Answer quickly, O Virgin” (Homilies in Praise of the Virgin Mother 4).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He sings that Mary conceived through her ear: the Word entered by hearing, as death had once entered Eve by listening to the serpent (Hymns on the Church).
magis: Lumen Gentium 56
Mary, consenting to the divine word, became the Mother of Jesus, freely cooperating in human salvation through faith and obedience.
Catechism 484–494
The Annunciation; Mary's faith and obedience; “Let it be done to me”.
saints: This week
7 December: St Ambrose. 8 December: Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2026-12-06.prayer: Lord God, you sent your angel to the Virgin of Nazareth, and through her yes your Word became flesh. Open the eyes of our hearts, pour your Spirit upon us, and make us, like Mary, servants who welcome your word and bring Christ to others. Amen.

2026-12-13.title: Third Sunday of Annunciation
2026-12-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: God confirms the promise to Abraham
Paul is called to make known the mystery of Christ
The birth of John the Baptist
2026-12-13.alt: Season of Annunciation. The 25 Days' Fast continues.
2026-12-13.verse: He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And all of them were amazed. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.
theo: The third Sunday of Annunciation celebrates a birth: John the Baptist. Elizabeth's neighbours and relatives hear “that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.” When the child is to be named, Elizabeth insists: “He is to be called John”, a name meaning “God has been gracious”. Zechariah, mute for nine months, writes it on a tablet, and at once his tongue is freed and he praises God.

The Old Testament readings prepare us. Abraham welcomes three mysterious visitors under the oaks of Mamre and hears the promise: “Your wife Sarah shall have a son.” The wife of Manoah, barren, is told by the angel that she will bear Samson, consecrated to God from birth, who “shall begin to deliver Israel.” These births are signs that God himself is preparing salvation. John is the last and greatest of them: the forerunner, consecrated from the womb, who will prepare the way of the Lord.

Paul speaks of “the mystery of Christ… that the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body.” He calls himself “the very least of all the saints”, yet entrusted with proclaiming “the boundless riches of Christ.” Like John, Paul's greatness lies in pointing to Christ.

The question of the crowd is ours: “What then will this child become?” Every child is a promise from God. Our families and parishes must help each child discover the hand of the Lord upon him or her. And Zechariah reminds us: when we finally obey God's word, our tongue is freed for praise.
conn: The name John.
Yôḥānān means “The Lord has been gracious”. The name itself announces the season: God's grace is about to appear (Titus 2:11).
Hospitality at Mamre.
Abraham's welcome of three visitors (Genesis 18) is read in Hebrews 13:2, “some have entertained angels without knowing it”, and in Eastern iconography as a figure of the Holy Trinity.
Nazirites from birth.
Samson (Judges 13:5) and John (Luke 1:15, no wine or strong drink) are both consecrated to God from the womb, as was Samuel (1 Samuel 1:11). John is the fulfilment of this line.
The tongue freed.
Zechariah's first words are the Benedictus (Luke 1:68–79), prayed every morning by the Church. His silence ends in a song.
altar: Zechariah's tongue was freed and he began to praise God. In the Qurbana we are invited to the same praise: after hearing the Word we answer with thanksgiving. John's name, “God is gracious”, is the meaning of every Eucharist: grace given, received, and returned in praise.
outline: Ask: what is the meaning of your name, and does your life live up to it?
From Abraham to Samson to John: God's promises come true.
Point 2 · “His name is John”: God is gracious
The name proclaims the season. Grace is the beginning of salvation.
Point 3 · What will this child become?
Every child is a promise. Families and parishes must help children find God's hand upon them.
Old Zechariah, after nine months of silence, singing aloud with a baby in his arms.
“The hand of the Lord was with him.”
live: Each night this week, trace the sign of the cross on your children's foreheads.
Welcome a guest, neighbour or stranger with Abraham's generosity.
End your daily silence of the fast with a short prayer of praise.
fathers: St Augustine
“John is the voice, Christ is the Word… The voice passes, the Word remains” (Sermon 293).
St Ambrose
Zechariah received back his speech when he wrote the name: “the voice of the father is freed by the birth of the voice” (Commentary on Luke 1).
magis: Catechism 523
John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor, sent to prepare his way; “more than a prophet”.
Catechism 2373
Children are a gift from God and the supreme gift of marriage.
saints: This week
14 December: St John of the Cross. 18 December: The Miraculous Cross at Mylapore.
2026-12-13.prayer: Lord God, faithful to your promises, you gave Zechariah and Elizabeth a son and named him John, for you are gracious. Bless the children of our families, lay your hand upon them, and free our tongues to praise you. Amen.

2026-12-20.title: Fourth Sunday of Annunciation
2026-12-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Isaac receives Rebekah according to the will of God
Discern the will of the Lord
God's intervention in the birth of Jesus: the annunciation to Joseph
2026-12-20.alt: Last Sunday of Annunciation. Christmas is on Friday 25 December.
2026-12-20.verse: When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife.
theo: The last Sunday before Christmas turns to St Joseph. Mary is found with child “from the Holy Spirit”, and Joseph, “a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly.” Then an angel speaks in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife… She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” Joseph wakes and does exactly what he is told. He never speaks a word in the Gospels; his faith is obedience.

The Old Testament readings show God at work in marriages and families. Rebekah is asked, “Will you go with this man?” and answers, “I will”; Isaac loves her and is comforted. Hannah, childless and mocked, pours out her soul before the Lord in the Temple; the priest Eli thinks she is drunk, but God hears her and gives Samuel. In both stories God's will is discovered and accepted in prayer.

Paul tells the Ephesians: “Understand what the will of the Lord is… be filled with the Spirit… giving thanks to God the Father at all times.” Joseph is the model: he does not know everything, but he discerns God's will and acts on it.

Through Joseph, son of David, Jesus is legally inserted into David's line; Joseph names him, gives him a home, protects him. On the threshold of Christmas the Church asks fathers, and all of us, to learn Joseph's silent, courageous obedience.
conn: “Do not be afraid.”
The angel's first words to Zechariah (Luke 1:13), to Mary (Luke 1:30), to Joseph (Matthew 1:20) and to the shepherds (Luke 2:10) are the same. God's coming begins by casting out fear.
Joseph the dreamer.
Like Joseph son of Jacob, who was guided by dreams and went down to Egypt (Genesis 37–50), Joseph of Nazareth receives God's guidance in dreams and takes the child to Egypt (Matthew 2:13).
The name Jesus.
Yeshua means “The Lord saves”. The angel explains: “for he will save his people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).
Hannah's song.
Hannah's later song (1 Samuel 2:1–10) is the model for Mary's Magnificat: God lifts up the lowly.
altar: Joseph received Mary and the child into his home. At the Qurbana we too receive Christ, not into a house but into ourselves. Joseph's silent reverence is a model for our preparation for Communion: wake up, do what the Lord commands, and take him home.
outline: Ask: when did God speak to you through an unexpected situation?
Rebekah's “I will”, Hannah's prayer: God works through marriages and mothers.
Joseph wants to protect Mary's dignity; justice joined to mercy.
Point 3 · He did as the angel commanded
Joseph's faith is obedience without a word. Fathers, learn from him.
Joseph waking in the night, rising and taking Mary home: the first Christmas preparation.
“Do not be afraid to take Mary into your home.”
live: Pray to St Joseph for the fathers in your family this week.
Bring one decision to prayer before acting.
Tell God honestly what troubles you, as Hannah did.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
Joseph showed “a wisdom free from passion”: he did not wish to expose Mary even before he understood the mystery (Homilies on Matthew 4).
St Ephrem the Syrian
In his hymns Joseph speaks to the infant: “How shall I, a poor man, carry the Lord of all?”, marvelling at the mystery he serves (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Pope Francis, Patris Corde (2020)
Joseph: beloved, tender, obedient, accepting, creatively courageous, a working father, a father in the shadows.
St John Paul II, Redemptoris Custos 3–4
Joseph's obedience of faith, parallel to Mary's.
saints: This week
25 December: Christmas. 26 December: St Stephen. 27 December: St John the Apostle; Holy Family.
2026-12-20.prayer: Lord God, you entrusted your Son to the care of St Joseph. Give us his faith, his silence and his courage, so that we may welcome Jesus and Mary into our homes this Christmas. Amen.

2026-12-25.title: Christmas – The Nativity of Our Lord (Yalda)
2026-12-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: The virgin shall bear a son; a child is born for us
The King who is to come from Bethlehem
God sent his Son, born of a woman
2026-12-25.alt: Solemnity of the Nativity of Our Lord; day of obligation. The season of Nativity (Yalda) begins.
2026-12-25.verse: But the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid; for see—I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people: to you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is the Messiah, the Lord.”
theo: “To you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is the Messiah, the Lord.” Christmas is not a sentimental story about a baby; it is the announcement that God has become man. The eternal Son, through whom all things were made, is born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem, laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn.

The prophets had promised it. Isaiah: “Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel”; and “a child has been born for us, a son given to us… Prince of Peace.” Micah: from little Bethlehem will come one “whose origin is from of old, from ancient days”, who will feed his flock and “be the one of peace.” Paul gathers it all: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman… so that we might receive adoption as children.”

The first to hear the news are shepherds, poor and on the margins. The sign given them is humble: “a child wrapped in bands of cloth and lying in a manger.” Heaven sings, “Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favours.” The shepherds go “with haste”, find the child, and return glorifying God. Mary “treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.”

The Syriac tradition loves to say that the One who feeds all creation lay in a feeding trough. Bethlehem, “house of bread”, gives us the Bread of Life. Christmas leads straight to the altar: the One born in a manger gives himself to us in the Holy Qurbana.
conn: The manger.
A manger is a feeding trough. The Fathers saw a sign: the One who would say “I am the bread of life” (John 6:35) is laid where animals eat.
Shepherds in David's town.
David was a shepherd of Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16:11). Shepherds are the first to greet the Son of David, the Good Shepherd (John 10:11).
Augustus and the census.
Augustus was hailed as “saviour” and bringer of peace. Luke deliberately sets Christ's birth under his decree: the true Saviour and Prince of Peace lies in a manger (Luke 2:1, 11).
The firstborn.

Luke calls Jesus Mary's “firstborn” (2:7), a legal title for the child who belongs to God (Exodus 13:2), not implying other children; Hebrews 1:6 calls Christ God's “firstborn” brought into the world.
altar: St Ephrem sings that the Bread of Life came down and was laid in a manger so that we might eat and live. At the Christmas Qurbana we kneel like the shepherds before the same Lord, now hidden under the sign of bread. Communion is our Christmas: Christ born in us.
outline: Begin with the angel's words: “Do not be afraid; I bring you good news of great joy for all the people.”
The eternal Son is born of the Virgin Mary. This is the heart of Christmas.
Point 2 · Good news for the poor
Shepherds, a manger, no room in the inn: God comes in humility, for everyone.
The Prince of Peace brings reconciliation; Christmas must change our relationships.
Mary pondering all these things in her heart, the Child in her arms.
“To you is born this day a Saviour.”
live: Kneel before the crib with your family and pray together.
Bring good news to the poor (Luke 2:10)
Share a Christmas meal or gift with a poor family.
fathers: St Leo the Great
“Our Saviour, dearly beloved, was born today: let us rejoice. There is no room for sadness on the birthday of life” (Sermon 21 on the Nativity).
St Ephrem the Syrian
“Blessed is the Shepherd who became a lamb for our atonement… the Bread who came down from heaven” (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 525–526
The mystery of Christmas: God's glory in the poverty of the manger; to become children of God we must be born from above.
Catechism 461–463
The Incarnation: the Word became flesh.
saints: Christmas octave
26 December: St Stephen. 27 December: St John the Apostle. 28 December: Holy Innocents (Holy Childhood Day).
2026-12-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Word made flesh, born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem, we adore you. Fill our hearts with the joy of the angels, the humility of the shepherds and the faith of Mary, and give peace to our families and to the world. Amen.

2026-12-27.title: First Sunday of Nativity · Feast of the Holy Family
2026-12-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: He created them male and female
The Holy Family flees to Egypt
2026-12-27.alt: Sunday readings (Second Sunday of Nativity in the 2024–25 calendar): Exodus 2:1–10; Isaiah 49:1–6; 2 Timothy 2:16–26; Luke 2:21–35 (the Presentation). 27 December is also the feast of St John the Apostle, patron's day of Mar John Vadakkel, Mar John Nellikunnel and Mar John Panamthottathil.
2026-12-27.verse: Then Joseph got up, took the child and his mother by night, and went to Egypt.
theo: Two days after Christmas the Church looks at the family in which the Son of God grew up. It was not an easy family life. Soon after the birth, the angel warns Joseph: “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt… for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.” The Holy Family become refugees. Later they return and settle in Nazareth, where Jesus grows up in an ordinary home.

The readings draw a picture of the family according to God. In the beginning God created humankind in his image, “male and female he created them”, and blessed them. Sirach teaches children to honour father and mother: “Those who honour their father atone for sins… My child, help your father in his old age.” Paul describes a home led by Christ: mutual love, respect, obedience, and parents who do not provoke their children.

The Holy Family is not a picture of a perfect family without problems. It is a family that faced poverty, danger, exile, misunderstanding and grief, and stayed together in faith. Joseph protected; Mary pondered; Jesus obeyed and grew “in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favour.”

On this feast we pray for our families, especially those under strain: migrant families separated by work abroad, families with sick members, broken families, and refugees. The Holy Family knows their road.
conn: Out of Egypt I called my son.
Matthew applies Hosea 11:1 to Jesus (Matthew 2:15): Jesus relives Israel's story, going down to Egypt and coming out, the true Son and new Israel.
Moses and Jesus.
Pharaoh killed Hebrew baby boys, but Moses was saved (Exodus 1–2); Herod killed the children of Bethlehem, but Jesus was saved. Jesus is the new Moses who will lead a new exodus.
The Nazarene.
“He will be called a Nazorean” (Matthew 2:23) may echo the netzer, the “branch” from Jesse's root (Isaiah 11:1). The obscure village of Nazareth hides the Messiah.
The fourth commandment.
Sirach 3 is a commentary on “Honour your father and your mother” (Exodus 20:12), the first commandment with a promise (Ephesians 6:2).
altar: The Holy Family gathered around Jesus. Each Sunday our families gather around the same Jesus at the altar. The family that prays and receives the Qurbana together learns the love that holds the Holy Family together.
outline: Ask: what holds your family together in hard times?
Point 1 · God's design for the family
Male and female in God's image, blessed to give life.
Sirach: care for parents, especially in old age.
Refugees in Egypt, ordinary life in Nazareth: faith holds them together.
Joseph leading a donkey by night, Mary holding the child: a family on the move, held by God.
“Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our family.”
live: Pray the evening family prayer together every day this week.
Visit, call or care for your elderly parents or grandparents.
Pray for families separated by work abroad and for refugees.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
He called the Christian home a “little church” (Homily on Ephesians 20).
St Paul VI at Nazareth (1964)
“Nazareth is a school… a lesson of silence, a lesson of family life, a lesson of work.”
magis: Amoris Laetitia 30
The Holy Family of Nazareth, with its trials, is a model for every family.
The Christian family; duties of children toward parents.
saints: 27 December
St John the Apostle and Evangelist, the beloved disciple who took Mary into his home.
2026-12-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you grew up in the Holy Family of Nazareth, through exile, poverty and ordinary work. Bless our families: keep us united in love, faithful in prayer, and caring for the elderly and the young. Jesus, Mary and Joseph, protect our homes. Amen.

2026-12-01.title: First Tuesday of Annunciation
2026-12-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Now is the moment to wake from sleep
Zechariah did not believe the angel
2026-12-01.alt: The 25 Days' Fast traditionally begins today.
2026-12-01.verse: Because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time, you will become mute, unable to speak, until the day these things occur.
theo: Paul's call fits the beginning of the fast: “You know what time it is, how it is now the moment for you to wake from sleep. For salvation is nearer to us now than when we became believers; the night is far gone, the day is near. Let us then lay aside the works of darkness and put on the armour of light… put on the Lord Jesus Christ.”

Zechariah asks for a sign: “How will I know that this is so?” Gabriel's answer is both a rebuke and a gift: he will be silent until the promise is fulfilled. His nine months of silence become a retreat. During this fast, a little silence, from screens, gossip and noise, can prepare us to speak praise at Christmas.
outline: Salvation is near; put on the armour of light.
He asked for proof instead of trusting the word.
Silence can become a school of faith and praise.
live: Choose one daily silence for the 25 days: no phone for an hour, no TV at dinner.
Pay one “debt of love” today: a visit, a call, an apology.
2026-12-01.prayer: Lord, wake me from sleep and clothe me with your light. Forgive my doubts, and let the silence of these days prepare my heart to sing your praise. Amen.
altar: The Nombu leads to the Holy Qurbana of Christmas. Each Qurbana during these days is a step towards the manger: we listen to the promise in the readings and receive the One who is coming.

2026-12-02.title: First Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Jesus is sent by the Father
2026-12-02.verse: And the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.
theo: Paul thanks God for the gifts given to the Corinthians as they “wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ,” and assures them: “God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son.” The whole Annunciation season rests on God's faithfulness.

Jesus speaks of the One who sent him: “The one who sent me is true… he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.” The Son's mission flows from the Father's love and is lived in constant obedience. Christmas is the arrival of the One sent; our joy is to be sent in turn.
outline: Ask: who has been faithful to you through everything?
He will strengthen you to the end.
Jesus comes from the Father and speaks the Father's words.
The Son always does what pleases the Father.
live: Recall one way God was faithful to you this year and thank him.
Before each decision today ask: does this please the Father?
2026-12-02.prayer: Faithful God, you called me into fellowship with your Son. As he always did what pleased you, let me do your will, knowing you never leave me alone. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana Christ unites us to his own communion with the Father. Receiving him, we are drawn into that life where no one is alone.

2026-12-03.title: First Thursday of Annunciation · St Francis Xavier
2026-12-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: There is no other God besides me
2026-12-03.alt: Weekday readings: 1 Timothy 4:11–16 (Be an example in holiness); Matthew 24:45–51 (Be vigilant).
2026-12-03.verse: And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.”
theo: St Francis Xavier (1506–1552), Jesuit companion of St Ignatius, arrived in Goa in 1542 and spent years among the fishing communities of the southern coast of India, including Travancore, teaching the catechism and baptising thousands. He went on to Malacca and Japan and died on the island of Sancian, within sight of China. His body rests in Goa. The Church honours him as patron of the missions.

The readings for his feast speak of mission: God's own people, holy to the Lord (Deuteronomy); the call to “all the ends of the earth” to turn and be saved (Isaiah); the apostle who is “poor, yet making many rich” (2 Corinthians); and the Twelve sent two by two with nothing but a staff (Mark). In this season of announcements, Xavier reminds us that the Good News must be announced to everyone.
outline: Ask: who brought the Gospel to the fishing villages of our coast?
Point 1 · Turn to me, all the ends of the earth
God's salvation is for every nation.
Point 2 · Poor, yet making many rich
Xavier gave up everything to give Christ.
Mission depends on God, not on resources.
live: Pray for Kerala missionaries serving in North India, Africa and elsewhere.
Let your words and conduct today announce Christ.
saints: St Francis Xavier (1506–1552)
Patron of missions; laboured in Goa, along the southern Indian coast, Malacca and Japan; body venerated in Goa.
2026-12-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, you sent St Francis Xavier to bring your Gospel to our land and to the East. Give us his zeal, his poverty and his love, and send labourers into your harvest. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we are sent: the dismissal is a mission. Like the Twelve, we leave the church carrying Christ to the ends of our own small worlds.

2026-12-04.title: First Friday of Annunciation · First Friday
2026-12-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Seek the things that are above
2026-12-04.alt: First Friday: devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
2026-12-04.verse: But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it.
theo: “If you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above… Set your minds on things that are above.” Paul asks the baptised to put to death what is earthly and to “clothe yourselves with the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its creator.”

Jesus tells his disciples that they are blessed: prophets and righteous people longed to see what they see. In the Annunciation season we stand where the prophets longed to stand, at the threshold of the Incarnation. On this First Friday we look at the Heart of the One the prophets longed to see.
outline: Ask: what do your eyes look at most during the day?
Raised with Christ, we set our hearts on heaven.
Point 2 · Put on the new self
Put off the old ways; be renewed in God's image.
We see what prophets longed to see: Christ.
live: Fast from one kind of screen content during these weeks.
Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament today.
2026-12-04.prayer: Sacred Heart of Jesus, the prophets longed to see you; I am blessed to know you. Lift my mind to the things above and renew me in your image. Amen.
altar: On First Fridays we honour the Sacred Heart pierced on the Cross. In the Holy Qurbana that same Heart is offered for us, and from it flows the grace that clothes us in the new self.

2026-12-05.title: First Saturday of Annunciation
2026-12-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
2026-12-05.verse: Jesus said to him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
theo: Paul asks the Galatians: did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by believing what you heard? “Those who believe are the descendants of Abraham.” Faith is the open hand that receives God's gift.

On the road to Jerusalem three would-be followers meet Jesus. To one he says, “The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head”; to another, “Let the dead bury their own dead”; to the third, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” Elisha burned his plough to follow Elijah. Discipleship is wholehearted; the Lord who comes at Christmas asks for an undivided heart.
outline: Ask: what makes you look back when following Christ?
We receive the Spirit by believing.
Point 2 · Nowhere to lay his head
Following Jesus means trusting, not securing.
Elisha burned his plough; disciples do not look back.
“I will follow you, Lord, without looking back.”
live: Give up one thing that keeps pulling you back from God.
Pray the Rosary today with Mary, the perfect disciple.
2026-12-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, you had nowhere to lay your head. Give me a faith that follows you without delay and without looking back, like Mary your mother. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we receive, not earn. We come with open hands, as children of Abraham by faith, and Christ gives himself freely.

2026-12-07.title: Second Monday of Annunciation · St Ambrose
2026-12-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Nothing is impossible for those who believe
2026-12-07.alt: For St Ambrose: Deuteronomy 7:1–11; Sirach 15:1–6; 2 Timothy 4:1–8; Luke 14:25–33.
2026-12-07.verse: If in my name you ask me for anything, I will do it.
theo: Paul's goal for the Church is maturity: “until all of us come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to maturity, to the measure of the full stature of Christ.” No longer “children, tossed to and fro”, but “speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head.”

Jesus promises that the one who believes in him will do the works he does, and even greater, and that whatever we ask in his name he will do. St Ambrose, bishop of Milan, lived this: chosen bishop while still a catechumen, he grew into a pastor of great faith who stood firm before emperors and led St Augustine to baptism.
outline: Ask: in what way is your faith still childish?
Faith must mature in truth and love.
Prayer in Jesus' name is powerful.
A pastor who grew into greatness and brought Augustine to Christ.
live: Read one page of the Catechism this week.
Bring one intention to Jesus with confidence today.
saints: St Ambrose (c. 340–397)
Bishop of Milan, Doctor of the Church, defender of the faith, who baptised St Augustine.
2026-12-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me to grow up into you in truth and love. Hear the prayers I make in your name, and give your Church pastors like St Ambrose. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the whole Body is built up into Christ the Head. Receiving him together, we grow into one mature people.

2026-12-08.title: Second Tuesday of Annunciation · Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary
2026-12-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: The virgin will bear a son
God has spoken to us by a Son
2026-12-08.alt: Weekday readings: 1 Thessalonians 5:5–11 (Children of light); Luke 10:21–24 (Revealed to infants).
2026-12-08.verse: For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name. His mercy is for those who fear him from generation to generation.
theo: On 8 December 1854 Pope Pius IX defined as a dogma revealed by God that “the most Blessed Virgin Mary, in the first instant of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin” (Ineffabilis Deus). Mary was redeemed too, but in a more sublime way: preserved rather than cleansed. The Eastern tradition has long honoured her as “all-holy” (Panagia) and “all-pure”.

The readings prepare a dwelling for the Word. Wisdom says: “The Creator of all things… chose the place for my tent. He said, ‘Make your dwelling in Jacob.’” Isaiah promises the sign of Immanuel, born of the young woman. Hebrews proclaims that “in these last days God has spoken to us by a Son,” who became like us in every respect. A pure dwelling was prepared for the Son of God: the Immaculate Virgin.

At the very beginning, after the Fall, God promised enmity between the serpent and the woman (Genesis 3:15). The Church sees in Mary the woman in whom the serpent never had a share. And in the Magnificat Mary herself gives the reason for her greatness: not her merits, but God's mercy. “He has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant… the Mighty One has done great things for me.”
For us the feast is a feast of hope: what God did in Mary at the beginning, he wants to accomplish in us at the end, presenting us “holy and blameless before him in love” (Ephesians 1:4).
conn: Full of grace.
Gabriel greets Mary as kecharitōmenē, “one who has been graced” (Luke 1:28): a perfect participle, describing a lasting state. The Church reads it as a sign of her fullness of grace from the start.
The new Eve.
St Irenaeus wrote that the knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by Mary's obedience (Against Heresies 3.22). The Immaculate Conception shows Mary as the new Eve, free from the start.
Wisdom's tent.
Sirach 24 speaks of Wisdom pitching its tent in Israel; John 1:14 says the Word “lived among us”, literally “pitched his tent”. Mary's womb was the first tent of the Word.
Lourdes, 1858.
Four years after the definition, the Lady at Lourdes told St Bernadette: “I am the Immaculate Conception.”
altar: Before Communion we pray to be made worthy of the holy Mysteries. The Immaculate Virgin was prepared to receive the Word in her body; at every Qurbana we receive the same Lord. Mary teaches us to prepare a clean heart for him through confession and love.
outline: Ask: what does it mean that Mary was “full of grace” from the first moment?
The dogma: Mary preserved from original sin in view of Christ's merits. She too was redeemed.
Point 2 · A dwelling for the Word
Wisdom's tent, Immanuel's mother: God prepared a pure home for his Son.
Point 3 · He has done great things
Mary's greatness is God's mercy, not her pride. The Magnificat is our song too.
Bernadette at Lourdes hearing: “I am the Immaculate Conception.”
“The Mighty One has done great things for me.”
live: Make a good confession before Christmas.
Pray it each evening this week.
Pray a decade of the Rosary for purity of heart for young people.
fathers: St Ephrem the Syrian
“You alone and your Mother are in every way all-beautiful; for there is no blemish in you, my Lord, and no stain in your Mother” (Carmina Nisibena 27).
St Irenaeus
“The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary” (Against Heresies 3.22.4).
magis: Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus (1854)
Definition of the Immaculate Conception.
Catechism 490–493
Mary, “full of grace”, preserved from original sin, the “all-holy”.
saints: 8 December
Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2026-12-08.prayer: O God, by the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary you prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son, preserving her from every stain in view of his death. Through her intercession, purify our hearts and make us holy and blameless in love. Amen.

2026-12-09.title: Second Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Behold the handmaid of the Lord
2026-12-09.verse: For nothing will be impossible with God.
theo: Paul blesses God who “chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.” God's plan for each of us began before we were born; our vocation is to say yes to it.

Mary's question, “How can this be?”, is not doubt but a desire to understand. The answer reveals the Holy Spirit's power and gives a sign, Elizabeth's pregnancy, “for nothing will be impossible with God.” Mary then gives herself completely: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.”
outline: Ask: what seems impossible in your life right now?
God's plan for you is older than the world.
Faith seeks understanding and then trusts.
God's power is greater than our limits.
live: Write down one “impossible” situation and pray over it daily.
Thank God for your state of life and renew your commitment.
2026-12-09.prayer: Father, you chose me in Christ before the foundation of the world. With Mary I give you my yes, for nothing is impossible with you. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Holy Spirit overshadows the gifts as he overshadowed Mary, and the Word becomes present among us. We answer with Mary: let it be done to me.

2026-12-10.title: Second Thursday of Annunciation
2026-12-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Love one another with mutual affection
2026-12-10.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: Having received the Word, Mary does not stay at home; she goes “with haste” into the hill country to serve her elderly cousin. When Elizabeth hears her greeting, the child John leaps in her womb and she is filled with the Holy Spirit: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb… And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?”

Paul's words describe Mary's visit: “Let love be genuine… love one another with mutual affection… rejoice with those who rejoice.” Faith that receives Christ becomes charity that carries him to others. The ark of the covenant once rested three months in the house of Obed-edom and brought blessing; Mary, the new ark, stays three months with Elizabeth.
outline: Ask: whom could you visit this Advent season?
Faith sets Mary on the road to serve.
Christ's presence brings joy and the Spirit.
Point 3 · Blessed is she who believed
Mary's faith is her deepest blessing.
live: Visit an elderly or lonely relative this week.
Celebrate someone else's good news sincerely today.
2026-12-10.prayer: Holy Mary, you hurried to serve Elizabeth and carried Jesus to her. Teach me to carry Christ to others with genuine love and joyful faith. Amen.
altar: Every Holy Qurbana is a Visitation: Christ comes to us hidden, and our hearts leap for joy. Then we carry him to others.

2026-12-11.title: Second Friday of Annunciation
2026-12-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
2026-12-11.verse: He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things.
theo: Mary's song celebrates a God who turns the world upside down: the proud scattered, the powerful brought down, the lowly lifted up, the hungry filled. It is not a political programme but the logic of the Kingdom, already visible in a poor girl of Nazareth who carries the Son of God.

Paul applies that logic to money: give according to what you have, so that there may be “a fair balance between your present abundance and their need.” As in the desert, “the one who had much did not have too much, and the one who had little did not have too little.” The 25 Days' Fast is meant to make room for such sharing.
outline: Ask: whom would Mary's song lift up in your town?
The Magnificat reverses the world's values.
What we save by fasting is given to the poor.
“He has filled the hungry with good things.”
live: Give the money saved by your fast to the poor.
2026-12-11.prayer: Holy God, you lift up the lowly and fill the hungry. Make my fasting generous and my heart humble, like Mary's. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Lord who became poor feeds us with his own life. Those who receive him are sent to feed the hungry.

2026-12-12.title: Second Saturday of Annunciation
2026-12-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Do not turn away from the living God
Your eye is the lamp of your body
2026-12-12.verse: Your eye is the lamp of your body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light.
theo: Hebrews warns: “Take care… that none of you may have an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called ‘today’.” The generation in the desert did not enter God's rest because of unbelief. Today is always the day to listen.

Jesus speaks of the eye as the lamp of the body: what we look at shapes what we become. “Consider whether the light in you is not darkness.” In the weeks before Christmas, guarding our eyes and hearts makes room for the true Light who is coming into the world.
outline: Ask: what fills your eyes each day?
Point 1 · Today, if you hear his voice
We need each other to stay faithful.
Point 3 · The lamp of the body
What we look at shapes our soul.
“Let the light in me not be darkness.”
live: Send a word of faith-filled encouragement to a friend.
2026-12-12.prayer: Lord, light of the world, keep my heart soft to your voice today, and fill my eyes and my whole being with your light. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the veil is opened and our eyes are turned to the altar. What we contemplate there fills the whole body with light.

2026-12-14.title: Third Monday of Annunciation · St John of the Cross
2026-12-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: A good tree bears good fruit
2026-12-14.alt: For St John of the Cross: 1 Corinthians 2:1–10; Luke 14:25–33.
2026-12-14.verse: The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good… for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
theo: Paul tells the Corinthians to “clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch… For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.” Sin tolerated in a community spreads like yeast; holiness requires decision.

Jesus teaches that each tree is known by its fruit, and words come from the heart's treasure. St John of the Cross, the Carmelite mystic, taught that the heart must be purified, even through dark nights, so that God alone may fill it. Before Christmas we ask: what is stored in my heart?
outline: Ask: what comes out of your mouth when you are tired or angry?
Point 1 · Clean out the old yeast
Sin must be removed, not tolerated.
Our deeds and words reveal our heart.
St John of the Cross: purification leads to union with God.
“Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.”
live: Watch your words today; replace one harsh word with a kind one.
Clean out the “old yeast” with a good confession.
saints: St John of the Cross (1542–1591)
Carmelite friar, reformer with St Teresa of Ávila, mystic and Doctor of the Church, author of The Dark Night and The Living Flame of Love.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord, purify my heart as you purified St John of the Cross, so that from its good treasure only good may come, and you alone may fill it. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana Christ our Passover is offered. We come to the altar with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, asking him to remove the old yeast of sin.

2026-12-15.title: Third Tuesday of Annunciation
2026-12-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Salvation is the gift of God
The kingdom of heaven has come near
2026-12-15.verse: This is the one of whom the prophet Isaiah spoke when he said, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’”
theo: “By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” Paul reminds us that we were dead through trespasses, and God, “rich in mercy”, made us alive with Christ. Salvation is gift; good works are the path God prepared for us to walk in.

John the Baptist appears in the wilderness: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” People confess their sins and are baptised in the Jordan. Repentance is not earning grace; it is opening the door to it. This week is a good time for the sacrament of confession.
outline: Ask: what valley must be filled, what mountain made low in your life?
Salvation is God's gift, not our achievement.
John calls us to turn back to God.
Make straight paths through confession and charity.
live: Make your Christmas confession this week.
Settle one crooked matter: a debt, a lie, a quarrel.
2026-12-15.prayer: God, rich in mercy, you saved me by grace. Give me true repentance and help me prepare the way for your Son. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the gift of God, not the result of our works. We come not because we are worthy, but because he who is rich in mercy invites us.

2026-12-16.title: Third Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Fidelity to the word of God
2026-12-16.verse: Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
theo: Paul thanks God that the Thessalonians received his preaching “not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word, which is also at work in you believers.” The word of God, received in faith, works in us.

Jesus teaches faithfulness in small things: honest dealings, trustworthy use of money, an undivided heart. “No slave can serve two masters… You cannot serve God and wealth.” As Christmas approaches, with its spending and celebrations, the Gospel asks whom we really serve.
outline: Ask: who is your master during the Christmas shopping season?
God's word received in faith transforms us.
God, not wealth, must rule our Christmas.
live: Spend less on yourself and give more to the poor this Christmas.
Read the Christmas Gospel (Luke 2:1–20) slowly this week.
2026-12-16.prayer: Lord, let your word work in me. Make me faithful in little things and free from the love of money, so that I serve you alone. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Word we hear becomes the Bread we receive. The word at work in us is nourished at the altar.

2026-12-17.title: Third Thursday of Annunciation
2026-12-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Those who have put on Christ
2026-12-17.verse: By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
theo: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Zechariah sings: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favourably on his people and redeemed them.” He sees God's ancient promises, to David, to Abraham, being fulfilled. Then he turns to his child: “And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High.” The song ends with an image of dawn: “the dawn from on high will break upon us.”

Paul tells the Galatians: “As many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ… you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.” The promises Zechariah sang about are ours through baptism. The Church sings his Benedictus every morning at dawn.
outline: Ask: what is your first prayer each morning?
Point 1 · God has visited his people
Point 2 · Prophet of the Most High
John prepares the way by teaching forgiveness.
Point 3 · The dawn from on high
Christ is the rising sun who brings light and peace.
“The dawn from on high will break upon us.”
live: Pray Zechariah's song each morning until Christmas.
Make peace with one person before Christmas.
2026-12-17.prayer: Blessed are you, Lord God of Israel, for you have visited and redeemed your people. Let the dawn from on high shine on all in darkness and guide our feet into the way of peace. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana there is one table and one Bread for all. Whoever is clothed in Christ in baptism is welcome at his altar.

2026-12-18.title: Third Friday of Annunciation · The Miraculous Cross at Mylapore
2026-12-18.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: God raised Jesus whom you crucified
Jesus the Way, the Truth and the Life
2026-12-18.alt: Weekday readings: Colossians 1:10–16 (Lead a life pleasing to the Lord); Mark 1:1–8 (One more powerful than I is coming).
2026-12-18.verse: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
theo: Today the Syro-Malabar calendar commemorates the Miraculous Cross at Mylapore. The ancient stone cross with a Pahlavi inscription, found on St Thomas Mount near Chennai in the sixteenth century and venerated in connection with the apostle Thomas, is one of the oldest Christian monuments in India. Tradition records that it showed miraculous signs during the Holy Qurbana. Whatever one makes of the reports, the cross itself witnesses to the antiquity of the faith of the St Thomas Christians, who honoured the Cross without a corpus as the sign of victory and life.

The readings unfold the meaning of the Cross. Moses strikes the rock and water flows; the Fathers saw this fulfilled when the soldier's lance opened Christ's side. Peter proclaims: “God has made him both Lord and Messiah, this Jesus whom you crucified.” Paul says Christ reconciled Jews and Gentiles “to God in one body through the cross.” And Jesus, about to go to his Passion, tells Thomas: “I am the way.” The Way passes through the Cross.
outline: Ask: what does the cross in your home mean to you?
The struck Rock is Christ; from his side flows life.
The Cross breaks down walls and reconciles.
Thomas asked the way; the Way is the crucified and risen Lord.
“We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, for by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.”
live: Pray before the cross in your home tonight as a family.
Reconcile with one person before Christmas.
saints: The Miraculous Cross at Mylapore (18 December)
The ancient Persian stone cross of St Thomas Mount, venerated by the St Thomas Christians; the Syro-Malabar Church keeps its memory today.
2026-12-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, you made peace through your Cross and opened the way to the Father. As our fathers in faith honoured your Cross, let us glory in it and walk your way to life. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana makes present the sacrifice of the Cross. From the altar, as from the struck rock, flows the living water of grace.

2026-12-19.title: Third Saturday of Annunciation
2026-12-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Chosen by the grace of God
The one who comes from above is above all
2026-12-19.verse: He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
theo: Paul tells how God “set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace” and “was pleased to reveal his Son to me.” His Gospel is not human invention but revelation. Like Jeremiah and John the Baptist, Paul was called from the womb.

John the Baptist testifies: “The one who comes from above is above all… He whom God has sent speaks the words of God.” As Christmas approaches, the Church contemplates the One who comes from above: not a teacher among teachers, but the Son into whose hands the Father has given all things.
outline: Ask: how did God reveal his Son to you?
Jesus comes from heaven and speaks God's words.
In Christ, God gives himself fully.
“The one who comes from above is above all.”
live: Thank God today for the grace of your baptism and vocation.
Set up the crib at home this weekend with the family.
2026-12-19.prayer: Father, you set us apart and called us by grace. Prepare our hearts to welcome your Son who comes from above and gives the Spirit without measure. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the One who comes from above comes down upon our altar. Whoever receives him with faith has eternal life.

2026-12-21.title: Fourth Monday of Annunciation
2026-12-21.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: In the beginning was the Word
2026-12-21.verse: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
theo: Four days before Christmas the Church reads the opening of John's Gospel. Before Bethlehem there is eternity: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God… All things came into being through him… The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.” The child in the manger is the eternal Son, Creator of all.

Paul asks the Ephesians to “pray in the Spirit at all times” and to pray for him, “that when I speak, a message may be given to me to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel.” In these last days of waiting, prayer prepares the heart to receive the Word made flesh.
outline: Ask: who is the child we will adore at Christmas?
The baby of Bethlehem is God from all eternity.
No darkness can overcome his light.
Prayer opens the heart to the Word.
live: Read the Prologue slowly each day until Christmas.
Turn short moments of the day into prayer.
2026-12-21.prayer: Eternal Word of the Father, light of every person, shine in my darkness and prepare my heart to welcome you at Christmas. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the eternal Word, through whom all things were made, comes to us under the form of bread. The light that shone in Bethlehem shines on our altar.

2026-12-22.title: Fourth Tuesday of Annunciation
2026-12-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: The Son of God born of a woman
The one who came to witness to the Light
2026-12-22.verse: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
theo: Paul gives the shortest Christmas creed: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” The eternal Son receives a human mother; and through him we receive adoption, so that the Spirit in our hearts cries “Abba! Father!” We are no longer slaves but children and heirs.

John's Prologue continues: John the Baptist “came as a witness to testify to the light.” The true light came to his own, “and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him… he gave power to become children of God.” Christmas is a choice: to receive or to refuse.
outline: Ask: what does it mean to you to call God “Abba, Father”?
God chose the moment; the Son was born of a woman.
Through Christ we are adopted children and heirs.
His own did not receive him; will we?
“To all who received him, he gave power to become children of God.”
live: Pray the Our Father slowly, savouring the word “Father”.
Make one concrete space in your Christmas for Christ: confession, prayer, the poor.
2026-12-22.prayer: Father, in the fullness of time you sent your Son, born of a woman, to make us your children. Let me receive him and live as your child. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we cry with the Spirit, Abba, Father, in the Our Father. Receiving the Son, we become children of God.

2026-12-23.title: Fourth Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
2026-12-23.alt: The readings for this day are not in the 2024–25 First Set calendar (in that year Christmas fell earlier in the week). Please consult the official 2026–27 Syro-Malabar calendar when it is published.
2026-12-23.verse: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
theo: Two days before Christmas the whole Church holds her breath. The long season of announcements, to Zechariah, to Mary, to Joseph, is ending. Isaiah's names for the Child gather all our hopes: Wonderful Counselor for our confusion, Mighty God for our weakness, Everlasting Father for our loneliness, Prince of Peace for our quarrels.
These last days are for quiet preparation: finishing the 25 Days' Fast well, making peace, going to confession, and preparing a place, in the home and in the heart, for the Child who comes.
outline: Ask: which of Isaiah's names for Jesus do you most need this year?
Confession, peace, and a welcoming heart.
“A child has been born for us.”
live: Reconcile with someone before Christmas Eve.
Pray before the crib at home tonight.
2026-12-23.prayer: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace: come and be born in our hearts and homes. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we exchange the sign of peace before approaching the altar. The Prince of Peace asks us to be reconciled before we receive him.

2026-12-24.title: Fourth Thursday of Annunciation · Christmas Eve
2026-12-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
2026-12-24.alt: The readings for this day are not in the 2024–25 First Set calendar. Please consult the official 2026–27 Syro-Malabar calendar. The Christmas night celebration follows this evening.
2026-12-24.verse: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
theo: On Christmas Eve the Church looks to Bethlehem, “one of the little clans of Judah”. God chooses the small: a little town, a poor couple, a manger. Bethlehem means “house of bread”; there the Bread of Life is born.

Tonight families gather, lamps and stars are lit, and the parish celebrates the night Qurbana. Let the noise of preparations give way, at least for a few moments, to silent adoration. The One whose origin is from ancient days comes as a baby who can be held.
outline: Ask: why did God choose little Bethlehem?
The Bread of Life is born in Bethlehem.
“From you shall come forth one who is to rule.”
live: Spend five minutes in silence before the crib tonight.
Call or visit someone who will be alone this Christmas.
2026-12-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, born in Bethlehem, the house of bread, come into our homes tonight. Let us adore you in silence and share your love with the lonely. Amen.
altar: Bethlehem, the house of bread, is fulfilled at our altar. The One laid in a manger is given to us in the Holy Qurbana of Christmas night.

2026-12-26.title: First Saturday of Nativity · St Stephen, Protomartyr
2026-12-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Whoever endures to the end will be saved
2026-12-26.alt: Weekday readings: 1 John 2:26–29 (Abide in him); John 1:19–29 (Here is the Lamb of God). The Saturday after Christmas is mapped from the First Saturday of Nativity in the 2024–25 calendar; please verify.
2026-12-26.verse: While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
theo: The day after Christmas the Church remembers St Stephen, the first martyr. It seems abrupt: from the crib to stones. But the Fathers saw the connection: yesterday Christ was born on earth so that today Stephen might be born into heaven. The Child came to give his life, and those who follow him share his self-giving.

Stephen, “full of grace and power”, sees “the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.” As he dies he prays like Jesus on the Cross: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit… Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” Among those approving his death is a young man named Saul, the future Paul. Forgiveness sown in blood bears fruit.
outline: Ask: why does the Church celebrate a martyr the day after Christmas?
Point 1 · Born on earth, born into heaven
Christ's birth leads to Stephen's martyrdom.
Point 2 · Full of grace and the Spirit
Stephen speaks with wisdom no one can withstand.
Stephen dies forgiving, like Jesus; Saul is converted.
“Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
live: Pray today for someone who has hurt you.
Remember Christians who suffer for their faith this Christmas.
saints: St Stephen, Protomartyr
One of the seven chosen to serve (Acts 6), the first to die for Christ, praying for his killers.
2026-12-26.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were born so that we might be born into heaven. Give us St Stephen's courage and his forgiving heart, and strengthen all who suffer for your name. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we receive the Christ for whom Stephen died. Strengthened by him, we too can forgive and endure.

2026-12-28.title: First Monday of Nativity · Holy Childhood Day (The Holy Innocents)
2026-12-28.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: A voice of lamentation in Ramah
2026-12-28.alt: Weekday readings (mapped; verify): Ephesians 4:7–12; Matthew 6:16–21. Holy Childhood Day (Thirubalasakhyam): the day of the Holy Childhood Association.
2026-12-28.verse: A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing and loud lamentation, Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be consoled, because they are no more.
theo: The joy of Christmas is followed by the tears of Bethlehem. Herod, furious at being tricked by the Magi, kills all the boys of Bethlehem two years old and under. Matthew hears in the mothers' cry the voice of Rachel weeping in Ramah. From Abel onward, innocent blood has cried out to God; the Holy Innocents are the first to die in place of Christ.

The Church honours them as martyrs who witnessed to Christ not by speaking but by dying. On this day Kerala's Church celebrates Holy Childhood Day: children praying and sharing for other children. We also remember all innocent children who suffer today: the unborn, abused, trafficked, hungry and war-torn. Jeremiah's promise stands: “there is hope for your future.”
outline: Ask: who are the innocents suffering today?
God hears the cry of the innocent.
The mothers of Bethlehem and of every age.
Holy Childhood: children praying and sharing for others.
live: Pray for unborn children and support a pro-life or child-care work.
Encourage children to share a gift for poor children.
saints: The Holy Innocents
The children of Bethlehem killed by Herod, honoured from the early centuries as martyrs.
2026-12-28.prayer: Lord Jesus, the Holy Innocents died in your place. Protect all children today, the unborn and the suffering, and console every weeping mother. Make our children generous for other children. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we offer the Lamb who was slain for all. The Holy Innocents, the first to die in his place, stand with him.

2026-12-29.title: First Tuesday of Nativity
2026-12-29.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: The boy Jesus in the Temple
2026-12-29.alt: Mapped from the weekday after the Sunday of Nativity in the 2024–25 calendar; please verify.
2026-12-29.verse: He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
theo: At twelve Jesus stays behind in the Temple; Mary and Joseph search for him for three days in anguish. When they find him, he answers: “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” Even as a boy he knows who his Father is. Then he goes down with them to Nazareth and is obedient to them, growing in wisdom and favour.

Paul gives the rule of Christian family and community life: “Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ… let us not grow weary in doing what is right… let us work for the good of all.” The home at Nazareth was such a place: love that carried, patience that waited, and obedience that grew.
outline: Ask: have you ever lost someone and searched in anguish?
Jesus' first recorded words reveal his identity.
The Son of God obeys his parents.
“I must be in my Father's house.”
live: Take on one burden for a family member this week.
Make a visit to church this week.
2026-12-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were found in your Father's house and lived obediently at Nazareth. Help us bear one another's burdens and grow in wisdom and grace. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we bring the burdens of others to the altar in the prayers of the faithful. Christ, who carried our burden on the Cross, carries them with us.

2026-12-30.title: First Wednesday of Nativity
2026-12-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: My grace is sufficient for you
2026-12-30.alt: Mapped from the 2024–25 calendar; please verify.
2026-12-30.verse: But he said to them, “It is I; do not be afraid.”
theo: Paul, burdened by a “thorn in the flesh”, begs the Lord three times to remove it and hears: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” He learns to boast of his weakness, “so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.”

The disciples row against the wind at night; Jesus comes to them walking on the sea and says, “It is I; do not be afraid.” As the year ends, many of us look back on storms and weaknesses. The Child of Bethlehem is the Lord of the storm; he comes to us in the dark and says the same words.
outline: Ask: what storm or weakness did you face this year?
God's power works through our limits.
Jesus comes to us in the dark.
Face the new year with trust.
“It is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Give God one weakness and ask for his grace.
Pray “Jesus, I trust in you” whenever anxious about the new year.
2026-12-30.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to your disciples in the storm and said, “It is I; do not be afraid.” Let your grace be sufficient for me, and your strength work in my weakness. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we receive the grace that is sufficient. The Lord who walked on the waters comes to us in our weakness.

2026-12-31.title: First Thursday of Nativity · End of the Year
2026-12-31.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Fight the good fight of the faith
Let us bear fruit: the fig tree given another year
2026-12-31.alt: Weekday readings (mapped; verify): Acts 3:20–26; Matthew 4:12–17. Many parishes hold a thanksgiving service at the year's end.
2026-12-31.verse: He replied, ‘Sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it. If it bears fruit next year, well and good; but if not, you can cut it down.’
theo: On the last day of the civil year the Church gives us a parable of mercy and urgency. A fig tree has borne no fruit for three years; the owner says, “Cut it down!” The gardener pleads: “Sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it.” The new year is that “one more year”: a gift of patience, and a call to bear fruit.

The other readings complete the picture: atonement and reconciliation (Leviticus), the passing of all things compared to the eternal reward of the righteous (Wisdom), and Paul's charge, “There is great gain in godliness combined with contentment… Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called.” Thank God for the year, ask pardon for its sins, and begin again.
outline: Ask: what fruit did my life bear this year?
God's patience gives us time to change.
Begin the new year with resolve and contentment.
“Let it alone for one more year.”
live: Write down ten blessings of this year and thank God as a family.
Make peace with God and choose one fruit to bear in the new year.
2026-12-31.prayer: Lord of time and eternity, we thank you for every blessing of this year and ask your pardon for our sins. Give us one more year of grace, and help us bear fruit for your glory. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana of the year's end we give thanks, the true meaning of ‘Eucharist’. The Gardener who pleads for us feeds us for the year to come.

quick: Mary's yes is the hinge of salvation history.
God opens blind eyes, as he did for Balaam.
Like Mary, we are called to hear the Word and carry him.
2026-12-06.action: Pray the Angelus at noon until Christmas.
2026-12-06.question: What is God asking me to say yes to?
2026-12-06.special: Second Sunday of Annunciation: the Gospel of the Annunciation to Mary.
illus: An illustration

In many Kerala parishes the church bell still rings at 6 am, noon and 6 pm, and older people stop wherever they are to pray the Angelus. In three short prayers they remember Nazareth: the angel's message, Mary's yes, and the Word made flesh.

family.explain: The angel Gabriel told Mary she would be the mother of Jesus. Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.” She said yes to God! We can say yes to God too.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always say yes to God, like Mary.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way you can say yes to God this week?”

kidsaint: A governor in Milan who was chosen as bishop by the people's cry before he was even baptised! He became a great preacher and helped St Augustine find Jesus. Lesson: God can call us in surprising ways; say yes like Mary.
term: Latin for “let it be done”, Mary's answer to the angel (Luke 1:38). In the Church's tradition the word sums up Mary's whole-hearted consent to God's plan.

pm.open: Lord God, in this season of Annunciation you speak to us through your messengers. As we gather, prepare our hearts to hear your word and to answer like Mary. Amen.
share: How has God spoken to me this week, through people, events or Scripture?
What makes it hard for me to say yes to God?
How can our family prepare a place for Jesus this Christmas?
pm.resp: Lord, let it be done according to your word.
interc: For the Church, that she may listen to God's word and answer with faith.
For mothers expecting a child this Christmas, that they may be protected.
For families preparing for Christmas, that they may prepare their hearts more than their houses.
For those who find it hard to believe, that God may give them signs of his love.
For our parish, that this Nombu may bear fruit in conversion and charity.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you came because Mary said yes. Help us say yes to you each day of this season, and bring us with joy to the feast of your birth. Amen.

quick: “John” means “God has been gracious”.
God keeps his promises from Abraham to John.
Every child is a promise: “What will this child become?”
2026-12-13.action: Bless your children each night this week.
2026-12-13.question: Do I see God's hand upon the children in my life?
2026-12-13.special: Third Sunday of Annunciation: the birth of John the Baptist.
illus: An illustration

In many Kerala families the grandfather or grandmother chooses a baptismal name with care, often a saint's name. Ask your children what their name means and whose name it is; it is the first gift of faith they received.

family.explain: When John was born, everyone was happy. His dad Zechariah had not been able to speak, but when he wrote “His name is John”, he could speak again and he praised God!
family.intention: We pray for all children, for expecting mothers, and for couples hoping for a child.
family.ask: Ask each child: “Do you know what your name means?”

catechism: John the Baptist, forerunner of the Lord.
The baptismal name; the dignity of each person's name.
kidsaint: Born when his parents were very old, John lived in the desert, ate locusts and wild honey, and told everyone to get ready for Jesus. He said: “He must increase, I must decrease.” Lesson: point others to Jesus, not to yourself.
term: John the Baptist's title: the one who runs ahead to prepare the way of the Lord (Luke 1:76), fulfilling Isaiah 40:3 and Malachi 3:1.

pm.open: Gracious God, you gave Zechariah and Elizabeth a son whose name means “God has been gracious”. As we gather, loosen our tongues for praise and open our hearts to your mercy. Amen.
share: The neighbours rejoiced with Elizabeth (Luke 1:58). When have I truly rejoiced at another person's blessing?
Zechariah's tongue was freed when he obeyed (Luke 1:63–64). What act of obedience would free me for praise?
The crowd asked: what then will this child become? (Luke 1:66). How do we help the children of our family discover God's hand upon them?
pm.resp: God has been gracious; we praise you, Lord.
interc: For the Church, that like John the Baptist she may always point to Christ.
For children, that they may grow in faith and discover God's call.
For parents, that they may raise their children as gifts from God.
For couples waiting for a child, that they may know God's mercy.
For our parish, that this Nombu may loosen our tongues for praise and witness.
pm.close: Lord God, you prepared the way for your Son through John the Baptist. Make us forerunners of Christ in our homes and workplaces, and fill our mouths with your praise. Amen.

quick: Joseph's faith is obedience without words.
God's will is found in prayer, as by Rebekah and Hannah.
“Do not be afraid”: God's coming casts out fear.
2026-12-20.action: Pray to St Joseph for the fathers in your family.
2026-12-20.question: What is God asking me to welcome into my home?
2026-12-20.special: Fourth Sunday of Annunciation: the annunciation to Joseph. Christmas is on Friday.
illus: An illustration

In 2020 Pope Francis wrote that St Joseph is the saint of the “hidden ones”: nurses, shop workers, cleaners, parents, grandparents, who keep the world going without being noticed. Joseph never speaks in the Gospels, yet without him the Christmas story would not stand.

family.explain: St Joseph was going to quietly leave Mary, but an angel told him in a dream to take care of Mary and baby Jesus. Joseph woke up and obeyed right away. He loved and protected the Holy Family.
family.intention: We pray for all fathers and grandfathers, and for families preparing for Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we take care of each other like St Joseph?”

catechism: The annunciation to Joseph; the name Jesus.
Jesus' obedience to Mary and Joseph in the hidden life.
kidsaint: A carpenter from Nazareth who loved Mary and Jesus. When God spoke to him in dreams, he obeyed at once, even taking his family to Egypt to keep Jesus safe. Lesson: obey God quickly and protect those you love.
term: Pope Francis's apostolic letter on St Joseph (8 December 2020), which opened a Year of St Joseph.

pm.open: Lord God, you entrusted your Son to the care of St Joseph. As we gather on this last Sunday before Christmas, give us Joseph's silent faith and courageous obedience. Amen.
share: Joseph planned to dismiss Mary quietly until the angel spoke (Matthew 1:19–20). When have I had to change my plans for God's plan?
Joseph did as the angel commanded (Matthew 1:24). What is God asking me to do that I hesitate over?
How can fathers in our families imitate St Joseph?
pm.resp: St Joseph, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that, like Joseph, she may protect Christ in the world.
For fathers, that they may be righteous, gentle and courageous like St Joseph.
For couples preparing for marriage, that, like Isaac and Rebekah, they may seek God's will.
For women who suffer like Hannah, that God may hear their prayer.
For our families, that we may welcome Christ this Christmas.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you were welcomed and protected by St Joseph. Through his prayers, make our homes places where you are welcomed, loved and protected. Amen.

quick: God has become man: to us is born a Saviour.
He comes in poverty, for everyone, beginning with the shepherds.
Bethlehem, house of bread, gives us the Bread of Life.
2026-12-25.action: Share a Christmas meal or gift with a poor family.
2026-12-25.question: Is there room for Jesus in my life this Christmas?
2026-12-25.special: Christmas: Solemnity of the Nativity of Our Lord, day of obligation. The season of Nativity (Yalda) begins.
illus: An illustration

In Kerala homes the Christmas star is hung on the veranda and lit at dusk. It is a small sign, but it tells everyone who passes: Christ is born, and this house welcomes him. The shepherds were guided by angels; our neighbours are guided by our light.

family.explain: Jesus, God's Son, was born as a little baby in Bethlehem and laid in a manger. Angels told poor shepherds, who came to see him. God came for everyone, especially the poor and the little.
family.intention: We pray for families without homes, for refugees, and for peace in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift can we give Jesus this Christmas?”

kidsaint: Poor men watching their sheep at night were the first to hear that Jesus was born. They ran to see him and then told everyone! Lesson: when you meet Jesus, share the good news.
term: Syriac for “birth”, the Nativity of the Lord. In the Syro-Malabar calendar the season of Annunciation–Nativity (Suvara–Yalda) celebrates the coming of Christ.

pm.open: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those whom he favours. Lord Jesus, born for us this day, we gather around your manger with joy. Amen.
share: The shepherds went with haste and found the child (Luke 2:16). What did I find at the manger this Christmas?
Mary treasured all these words (Luke 2:19). What word of Christmas will I treasure in my heart?
How will I share the joy of Christmas with someone poor or alone?
pm.resp: Glory to God in the highest.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim to all the good news of great joy.
For peace in the world, especially in the Holy Land.
For families, that the Child of Bethlehem may dwell in their homes.
For the poor, the homeless and refugees, who share the poverty of the manger.
For all who are sick, lonely or grieving on this day.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you were born for us in Bethlehem. Fill our hearts with the joy of the shepherds, the faith of Mary and the peace of the angels' song. Amen.

quick: The Holy Family faced danger, exile and ordinary toil, together in faith.
God's design: man and woman in his image, blessed to give life.
