Honour father and mother, especially in old age.
2026-12-27.action: Pray together as a family every evening this week.
2026-12-27.question: How can my family become more like the Holy Family?
2026-12-27.special: Feast of the Holy Family (Sunday after Christmas). Also St John the Apostle.
illus: An illustration

Many Kerala families have a father or mother working in the Gulf, seeing their children once a year. The Holy Family knew separation and exile in Egypt. Faith, prayer and love kept them one; the same can keep our families one across the seas.

family.explain: Jesus' family had to run away to Egypt to keep baby Jesus safe. Later they came back and lived in Nazareth. Even when life was hard, they loved and protected each other.
family.intention: We pray for our family and for all families that are apart or in trouble.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do to make our home happier?”

catechism: The Christian family as domestic church.
kidsaint: The youngest apostle, called “the disciple whom Jesus loved”. At the Cross Jesus gave Mary to John as his mother, and John took her into his home. Lesson: love Jesus and take Mary into your family.
term: The Christian family, called a “little church” because faith is first lived, prayed and handed on at home (Lumen Gentium 11).

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you grew up in the home of Mary and Joseph in Nazareth. As we gather on the feast of the Holy Family, bless our families and make them homes of faith and love. Amen.
share: The Holy Family fled as refugees (Matthew 2:14). What hardships has my family faced, and how did faith help us?
Sirach says: help your father in his old age (Sirach 3:12). How do I care for my parents?
Paul says: parents, do not provoke your children (Colossians 3:21). What would make our home more peaceful?
pm.resp: Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our family.
interc: For all families, that they may imitate the Holy Family of Nazareth.
For families separated by migration, that love may keep them united.
For refugees, who share the road of the Holy Family into Egypt.
For elderly parents, that they may be honoured and cared for by their children.
For broken families, that they may find healing and reconciliation.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave your Son a home in Nazareth with Mary and Joseph. Bless our families with their faith, their love and their courage, and keep us united in you. Amen.

quick: Now is the moment to wake from sleep.
Zechariah doubted and became silent.
Silence can prepare us for praise.
2026-12-01.action: Choose one daily silence for the 25 Days' Fast.
2026-12-01.question: What noise keeps me from hearing God?

family.explain: Paul tells us it is time to wake up, because Jesus is coming. We prepare for Christmas by putting away bad habits and putting on Jesus, like new clothes.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may keep the Christmas fast with joy and love.
family.ask: Ask: “What one thing will each of us give up, and what one good thing will we do, during this Nombu?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to wake from sleep and to put on your light. As we begin the Christmas fast, open our ears to your word and our hearts to your coming. Amen.
share: Paul says the night is far gone and the day is near (Romans 13:12). In what area of my life am I still half asleep?
Zechariah could not speak for nine months. What noise could I give up this Nombu to listen to God?
What fast from food, and what fast from sin, will I keep until Christmas?
pm.resp: Lord, wake us and make us ready.
interc: For the holy Church, that she may keep this fast with faith and prepare a worthy dwelling for the Lord.
For our families, that the Nombu may bring more prayer, peace and charity into our homes.
For those who are addicted to alcohol, drugs or screens, that the Lord may set them free.
For couples who long for a child, like Zechariah and Elizabeth, that they may know God's tenderness.
For the poor, that our fasting may become food for them.
pm.close: Lord God, you heard the prayer of Zechariah and made his silence fruitful. Bless our fast, purify our hearts and make us ready to welcome your Son with joy at Christmas. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in Thrissur decided one Nombu to keep the television off in the evenings. The first week the children complained. By the third week they were telling Bible stories at the dinner table and the family rosary had become the best part of the day. The fast had made room.

quick: God is faithful.
Jesus is the One sent by the Father.
We are never alone when we do the Father's will.
2026-12-02.action: Thank God for one sign of his faithfulness this year.
2026-12-02.question: Do my choices please the Father?

family.explain: Jesus said: my Father is always with me, because I do what pleases him. God is with us too, especially when we do good.
family.intention: We pray for lonely people: grandparents, migrants and the sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Who do we know who is lonely, and how can we show them they are not alone?”

pm.open: Faithful Father, you never leave your children alone. Gather us in your Son's name, speak to us through your word, and make us faithful as you are faithful. Amen.
share: Paul says: God is faithful (1 Corinthians 1:9). When have I experienced God's faithfulness?
Jesus says: I always do what is pleasing to him (John 8:29). What would please the Father in my life this week?
Who around me feels alone, and what can I do for them?
pm.resp: Faithful God, stay with us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's faithfulness to every generation.
For those who feel abandoned, that they may experience the Father's presence.
For migrants and families separated by distance, that love may bridge the miles.
For the sick in hospitals and at home, that they may be comforted.
For our prayer group, that we may grow in fidelity to God's will.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you lived in constant communion with the Father. Keep us united to you, make us faithful in small things, and let no one around us feel alone. Amen.

illus: An illustration

An elderly widow in Kottayam, whose children were all abroad, said: “Every evening at six I sit before the picture of the Sacred Heart and tell him about my day. I am never alone.” Faith had turned her loneliness into communion.

quick: St Francis Xavier carried the Gospel along India's southern coast.
God's salvation is for all the ends of the earth.
Mission depends on God's power, not on resources.
2026-12-03.question: Whom am I called to bring the Good News to?

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends two by two to tell people about God. St Francis Xavier came all the way to India to tell people about Jesus. We can tell others about Jesus too.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, especially priests and sisters from Kerala working far away.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family help someone know Jesus this week?”

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, you sent your apostles to the ends of the earth and brought St Francis Xavier to our shores. Send your Spirit upon us as we gather, and make us missionaries of your love. Amen.
share: Paul says the apostles were poor yet made many rich (2 Corinthians 6:10). What riches of faith did missionaries bring to my family?
Jesus sent the Twelve with nothing (Mark 6:8). What do I rely on more than God?
Where is my mission field this week?
pm.resp: Lord, send us to proclaim your love.
interc: For missionaries throughout the world, especially those from our Church, that they may be strengthened.
For the people of the coastal regions of India, who received the faith through St Francis Xavier.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life in our families.
For Christians working abroad, that they may be witnesses of Christ in their workplaces.
For those who have never heard the Gospel, that they may come to know Christ.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you made St Francis Xavier a herald of the Gospel in our land. Through his prayers, give us his zeal and his joy, and make our lives a proclamation of your love. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Kerala working in a hospital in the Gulf was asked by a dying patient why she was always so gentle. She said simply: “Because Jesus is gentle with me.” That night the patient asked her to pray for him. Mission happens wherever a Christian lives the Gospel.

quick: Seek the things that are above.
Put off the old self; put on the new.
We are blessed to see what prophets longed to see.
2026-12-04.question: What do my eyes seek most?

family.explain: Paul tells us to put on kindness, humility, patience and forgiveness, like clothes we wear every day.
family.intention: We pray for our family on this First Friday, that the Sacred Heart of Jesus may make us kind and forgiving.
family.ask: Ask: “Which ‘clothes’ of kindness will each of us wear this week?”

pm.open: Sacred Heart of Jesus, on this First Friday we gather before you. Open our eyes to see your love and our ears to hear your word, and clothe us with the new life you won for us. Amen.
share: Paul says: seek the things that are above (Colossians 3:1). What earthly worry takes too much of my heart?
Which old garment of sin do I need to take off in confession this Nombu?
Jesus says: blessed are your eyes (Matthew 13:16). How have I seen God at work in my life this year?
pm.resp: Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may always set her heart on Christ and seek the things above.
For sinners, that the love of the Sacred Heart may draw them to confession this season.
For families broken by anger and harsh words, that they may put on kindness and forgiveness.
For those who have lost faith, that their eyes may be opened.
For all who suffer, that they may find rest in the Heart of Jesus.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, your Heart was pierced for us. Make our hearts like yours: humble, gentle, forgiving. Keep our minds on the things above, and bring us one day to the place you have prepared for us. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young man who had stopped going to church came back one First Friday because his mother was ill and had asked him to go in her place. He sat at the back. The Gospel that day said: blessed are your eyes, for they see. He later said: “That day I saw. I went to confession after twelve years.”

quick: We receive the Spirit by faith.
Following Jesus means trusting, not securing ourselves.
Disciples put their hand to the plough and do not look back.
2026-12-05.action: Give up one thing that pulls you back from God.
2026-12-05.question: What makes me look back?

family.explain: Jesus wants us to follow him right away, not later. When we plough a field we look ahead, not behind.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who keeps postponing their return to God.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing have we been putting off that we can do this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to follow you without delay. Gather us now, give us faith like Abraham, and help us put our hand to the plough without looking back. Amen.
share: Paul says we receive the Spirit by faith, not by works (Galatians 3:2). Do I sometimes try to earn God's love?
What am I postponing that God is asking me to do now?
What in my past still makes me look back instead of forward?
pm.resp: Lord, we will follow you.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim salvation as God's free gift.
For those who feel they are never good enough, that they may know God's love.
For young people choosing their vocation, that they may follow Christ generously.
For those weighed down by the past, that they may be healed and look forward with hope.
For our prayer group, that we may not delay our conversion.
pm.close: Lord God, you justified Abraham by faith and you call us to follow your Son. Free us from fear and delay, and make us faithful disciples who never look back. Amen.

illus: An illustration

An old farmer in Kuttanad used to tell young men learning to plough: “Fix your eye on a coconut tree at the end of the field and walk towards it. If you look at your feet or behind you, the line will bend.” Jesus is the tree at the end of our field.

quick: Faith must grow to maturity in Christ.
Ask in Jesus' name with confidence.
St Ambrose grew from catechumen to great pastor.
2026-12-07.action: Read one page of the Catechism this week.
2026-12-07.question: Where is my faith still childish?

family.explain: Paul tells us to grow strong in faith so that we are not blown around like a leaf in the wind. We grow by prayer, learning and love.
family.intention: We pray for young people in our family, that their faith may grow strong and deep.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do to learn more about our faith this month?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Head of the Church, you want us to grow to full maturity in you. As we gather, root us in your word and teach us to speak the truth in love. Amen.
share: Paul warns against being tossed by every wind of doctrine (Ephesians 4:14). Which ‘winds’ unsettle my faith today?
How do I speak the truth in love, especially in family arguments?
What step will I take to grow in knowledge of the faith?
pm.resp: Lord, make our faith strong.
interc: For the Church, that she may grow in unity and maturity.
For bishops and teachers of the faith, that like St Ambrose they may speak the truth with courage and love.
For young people confused by many voices, that they may find Christ.
For families divided by arguments, that they may learn to speak the truth in love.
For our parish, that we may grow together into the full stature of Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave St Ambrose wisdom and courage to guide your people. Give us a mature faith, rooted in your Son, so that we may not be shaken but grow in love. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A coconut seedling planted in loose sand falls over in the first monsoon wind. One planted deep, with good soil around its roots, bends but stands. Our faith needs deep roots before the winds come.

quick: Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment, in view of Christ's merits.
God prepared a pure dwelling for his Son.
Mary's greatness is God's mercy: “He has done great things for me.”
2026-12-08.action: Make a good confession before Christmas.
2026-12-08.question: How am I preparing a clean heart for Christ?
2026-12-08.special: Feast of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary (dogma defined by Pius IX, 8 December 1854).
illus: An illustration

When a family in Kerala expects an important guest, the house is cleaned, the floor washed, the best mat spread out. God prepared a home for his Son long before he came: a Virgin kept pure from the first moment of her life.

family.explain: God kept Mary free from all sin from the very beginning so that she could be Jesus' mother. Mary sang that God did great things for her. God wants to make our hearts clean too.
family.intention: We pray for pure hearts for our family, especially for the children and young people.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make our hearts clean for Jesus this Christmas?”

term: Not the virginal conception of Jesus, but Mary's own conception in her mother's womb, preserved from original sin by God's grace in view of Christ's merits (Ineffabilis Deus, 1854).

pm.open: Holy Mary, conceived without sin, you were prepared by God to be the dwelling of his Son. Pray with us as we gather, that our hearts too may be made ready for him. Amen.
share: Mary was full of grace from the first moment. What does it mean to me that grace comes before effort?
What sin keeps my heart from being a clean dwelling for Jesus?
How can I imitate Mary's purity of heart this Nombu?
pm.resp: Immaculate Mother, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that, like Mary, she may be holy and without blemish.
For children and young people, that they may grow in purity of heart.
For those trapped in sin, that the grace of God may set them free.
For mothers, that Mary may guide and protect them.
For our parish, that we may prepare a pure dwelling for Christ this Christmas.
pm.close: God our Father, you preserved the Virgin Mary from every stain of sin. Through her prayers, purify our hearts and make them a worthy home for your Son. Amen.

quick: God chose us in Christ before the world began.
Mary's question seeks understanding, not proof.
Nothing is impossible with God.
2026-12-09.question: What seems impossible to me, and have I given it to God?

family.explain: Mary did not understand everything, but she trusted God and said yes. Nothing is impossible for God.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family facing something that seems impossible.
family.ask: Ask: “Where does God want each of us to say yes this week?”

pm.open: Blessed be God, who chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. As we gather, give us Mary's trust and Mary's yes. Amen.
share: Paul says God chose me before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:4). How does that change the way I see myself?
Mary asked: how can this be? (Luke 1:34). What question do I bring to God today?
Where is God asking for my yes?
pm.resp: Here am I, Lord; let it be done according to your word.
interc: For the Church, that, like Mary, she may always say yes to God.
For those facing impossible situations: illness, debt, broken relationships, that they may trust God.
For young people discerning their vocation, that they may hear God's call.
For couples longing for children, like Elizabeth.
For all of us, that this Christmas God's word may take flesh in our lives.
pm.close: Lord God, you chose us before the world was made and you call us to share your life. With Mary, we say: here am I. Do with us according to your word. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young woman from a poor family in Idukki felt called to become a nurse but had no money for the course. Her parish priest helped her find a scholarship. Years later, as head nurse in a large hospital, she said: “I asked God: how can this be? He answered through people.” Nothing is impossible with God.

quick: Mary went with haste to serve.
Christ's presence brings joy: John leaped in the womb.
Blessed is she who believed.
2026-12-10.action: Visit an elderly or lonely relative this week.
2026-12-10.question: Whom is God asking me to visit?

family.explain: Mary hurried to help her cousin Elizabeth. When she arrived, baby John jumped for joy because Jesus was near.
family.intention: We pray for people who need a visit: the sick, the old, the lonely and new mothers.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can our family visit before Christmas?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, hidden in Mary's womb you brought joy to Elizabeth's home. Come into our gathering, fill us with your Spirit, and send us to visit others with love. Amen.
share: Mary went with haste to help (Luke 1:39). What makes me slow to help others?
Paul says: rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep (Romans 12:15). Whom do I need to accompany now?
Whom will I visit before Christmas?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bearers of your joy.
interc: For the Church, that she may go out in haste to serve those in need.
For pregnant mothers and their babies, that they may be safe and joyful.
For the elderly and lonely, that they may receive visits of love this Christmas.
For those who are grieving, that they may be comforted.
For our prayer group, that we may love one another with genuine affection.
pm.close: Lord God, you sent Mary with haste to serve Elizabeth. Make our love genuine and active, and let our visits carry your Son to all who need him. Amen.

illus: An illustration

In a village near Pala, a group of mothers began visiting new mothers in the parish for the first forty days after birth, bringing food and helping with housework. One young mother said: “I felt as if Mary herself had come to my house.”

quick: Mary's song reverses the world's values.
Christian giving seeks a fair balance.
Fasting makes room for sharing.
2026-12-11.action: Give what you save by fasting to the poor.
2026-12-11.question: How does my fasting help someone in need?

family.explain: Mary sang a song of joy because God loves the humble and feeds the hungry.
family.intention: We pray for families who will not have enough food this Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we save during this Nombu to give to the poor?”

pm.open: Holy Mary, your soul magnified the Lord. As we gather, teach us your song, give us humble hearts and open our hands to the poor. Amen.
share: Mary says God has looked on her lowliness (Luke 1:48). Do I see my smallness as a gift or as a shame?
Paul speaks of a fair balance (2 Corinthians 8:14). Where is my abundance, and who is in need near me?
How will I make my fast become food for the poor?
pm.resp: My soul magnifies the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may always stand with the poor and the humble.
For the hungry, the homeless and refugees this Christmas.
For the rich and powerful, that they may use their gifts with justice.
For all who feel small and forgotten, that they may know God looks on them with favour.
For our parish charity works, that they may be generous and wise.
pm.close: Lord God, you lifted up the lowly and filled the hungry with good things. Make us humble like Mary and generous like your Son, who became poor for our sake. Amen.

illus: An illustration

In many old Syro-Malabar homes there was a small clay pot called the pidiyari pot, into which the mother put a handful of rice before cooking each meal. At the end of the week the rice was given to the poor or to the church. Small handfuls fed many.

quick: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your heart.
Encourage one another every day.
The eye is the lamp of the body.
2026-12-12.action: Encourage a friend in faith today.
2026-12-12.question: What am I letting into my eyes and heart?

family.explain: Jesus says our eyes are like a lamp. When we look at good things, our hearts are full of light.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may use our phones and screens wisely.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we spend less time on screens and more time together this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, fill our eyes and hearts with your light. As we gather today, soften our hearts and teach us to encourage one another. Amen.
share: Hebrews warns against a hardened heart (Hebrews 3:12). Where has my heart grown cold?
What do my eyes look at most each day, and does it bring light or darkness?
Whom will I encourage in faith this week?
pm.resp: Lord, fill us with your light.
interc: For the Church, that her members may encourage one another daily in faith.
For those who have drifted away from God, that their hearts may be softened.
For young people addicted to screens and impure images, that they may be set free.
For families, that they may spend time together in love and prayer.
For our prayer group, that we may be a support to one another.
pm.close: Lord God, you speak to us today. Keep our hearts from hardening, guard the lamp of our eyes, and make us a community that encourages one another until your Son comes. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Changanacherry noticed her grandson spending every evening on his phone in his room. Instead of scolding, she asked him to help her read the Bible because her eyes were weak. Slowly the evenings changed. Encouragement worked where criticism had failed.

quick: Clean out the old yeast.
Each tree is known by its fruit.
Our words reveal our heart.
2026-12-14.action: Replace one harsh word with a kind one today.
2026-12-14.question: What treasure is stored in my heart?

family.explain: Jesus says a good tree gives good fruit. When our hearts are good, our words and actions are good too.
family.intention: We pray that our family may speak kind words at home.
family.ask: Ask: “What good ‘fruit’ did each of us give today?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our Passover Lamb, cleanse us of the old yeast of sin. As we gather, make our hearts good trees that bear good fruit. Amen.
share: Paul says a little yeast leavens the whole batch (1 Corinthians 5:6). What small sin am I tolerating that could spread?
Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks (Luke 6:45). What do my words reveal about my heart?
What will I bring to confession before Christmas?
pm.resp: Create in us a clean heart, O God.
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy and sincere in all her members.
For those trapped in sinful relationships and habits, that they may find the courage to change.
For Carmelites and all contemplatives, that through the prayers of St John of the Cross they may be filled with God.
For families, that their homes may be free of harsh words.
For all of us, that we may make a good confession this Nombu.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave St John of the Cross a love that grew even in darkness. Purify our hearts, make our words good fruit, and prepare us to celebrate your Son's birth with sincerity and truth. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A farmer in Wayanad had a mango tree that gave sour, wormy fruit. Instead of cutting it down, he grafted a good branch onto the old trunk. In two years it bore sweet mangoes. Grace is God's graft on our old nature.

quick: We are saved by grace through faith.
John calls us to repent.
Prepare the way through confession.
2026-12-15.action: Make your Christmas confession this week.
2026-12-15.question: What crooked path must I straighten for the Lord?

family.explain: God loves us so much that he saves us as a gift. We do good things not to earn his love, but because we already have it.
family.intention: We pray for someone in our family who has gone far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “What good work has God prepared for us to do this week?”

pm.open: God, rich in mercy, you made us alive in Christ when we were dead in sin. Gather us in thanksgiving and make us ready to do the good works you have prepared for us. Amen.
share: Paul writes: but God, who is rich in mercy (Ephesians 2:4). Where have I seen God bring life out of death?
Do I sometimes think I must earn God's love?
John called for repentance (Matthew 3:2). What do I need to turn away from?
pm.resp: By grace we have been saved; thanks be to God.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's mercy to all who feel dead in sin.
For family members who have left the faith, that they may return.
For those battling addiction, that God's grace may raise them up.
For penitents preparing for Christmas confession, that they may experience God's mercy.
For all of us, that we may walk in the good works God has prepared.
pm.close: Lord God, you raised us with Christ by grace. Let us never boast of ourselves, but give thanks always, and walk in the good works you prepared for us. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A father in Kollam had given up on his son, who had left home after years of drinking. One Christmas the son walked into the midnight Qurbana, thin and ashamed, and knelt at the back. After Mass he went to confession. His father later said: “I had written him off. But God had not.”

quick: God's word works in those who believe.
Faithful in little, faithful in much.
No one can serve God and wealth.
2026-12-16.action: Give more to the poor than to yourself this Christmas.
2026-12-16.question: Whom do I serve during this season?

family.explain: Jesus says if we are honest in small things, we will be honest in big things. We cannot love God and money both as masters.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always be honest.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can each of us do faithfully this week?”

pm.open: Lord, your word is at work in us who believe. As we gather, let us receive it not as a human word but as your own living word. Amen.
share: Paul says the word is at work in believers (1 Thessalonians 2:13). How has God's word worked in me this year?
Jesus speaks of faithfulness in very little (Luke 16:10). Where am I unfaithful in small things?
Am I serving God or wealth in my daily decisions?
pm.resp: Speak, Lord, your servants are listening.
interc: For the Church, that she may receive and proclaim God's word faithfully.
For those who suffer for their faithfulness to the Gospel.
For business people and workers, that they may be honest in all dealings.
For students, that they may be faithful in study and integrity.
For our prayer group, that God's word may bear fruit in us.
pm.close: Lord God, your word is living and active. Make us faithful in little things and in great, and let your word take flesh in our lives this Christmas. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A shopkeeper in Ernakulam was offered a large order if he would write a false bill for the customer's company. He refused and lost the order. A year later the same customer came back: “I want a supplier I can trust.” Faithfulness in small things became much.

quick: God has visited and redeemed his people.
John prepares the way through forgiveness.
Christ is the dawn from on high.
2026-12-17.action: Make peace with one person before Christmas.
2026-12-17.question: Where do I need the dawn of Christ's light?

family.explain: Zechariah sang a song of thanks when John was born. He said Jesus would come like the morning sun to chase away darkness.
family.intention: We pray for people who are treated as less important because of their caste, colour or poverty.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we treat everyone as a child of God?”

pm.open: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has visited and redeemed his people. As we gather, clothe us with Christ and let the dawn from on high break upon us. Amen.
share: Paul says there is no longer Jew or Greek, slave or free (Galatians 3:28). What divisions still exist in my heart or community?
Zechariah sings of serving God without fear (Luke 1:74). What fear keeps me from serving God?
Where do I need the dawn from on high to break into my darkness?
pm.resp: Blessed be the Lord, who has visited his people.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home where all are one in Christ.
For those who suffer discrimination by caste, race or poverty.
For the newly baptised, that they may live clothed in Christ.
For those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For our families, that we may pray the Benedictus with grateful hearts.
pm.close: Lord God, by your tender mercy the dawn from on high is breaking upon us. Clothe us with Christ, make us one, and guide our feet into the way of peace. Amen.

illus: An illustration

In an old parish in central Kerala, the parish priest invited the families of the colony, long kept at the edges, to carry the Christmas crib in the procession. Some parishioners grumbled. But that Christmas the whole parish sang together around one crib. All were one in Christ.

quick: The ancient Mylapore cross witnesses to the antiquity of our faith.
From the struck Rock, Christ, flows life.
The Cross is the way to peace and to the Father.
2026-12-18.action: Pray before the cross at home tonight.
2026-12-18.question: Do I see the Cross as a sign of victory and life?

family.explain: Jesus told Thomas: I am the Way. Our Mar Thoma cross reminds us that Jesus' Cross leads to new life, like a tree that blossoms.
family.intention: We pray for all St Thomas Christians in India and around the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Where is the Mar Thoma cross in our home, and what does it teach us?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, by your Cross you reconciled us to God and to one another. As we gather before the sign of your victory, quench our thirst with the living water of your Spirit. Amen.
share: The rock struck in the desert gave water (Exodus 17:6). What suffering in my life could become a source of grace?
Jesus says: do not let your hearts be troubled (John 14:1). What troubles my heart today?
How does the Cross unite what is divided in my family or community?
pm.resp: We adore you, O Christ, for by your Cross you have redeemed the world.
interc: For the St Thomas Christians in India and the diaspora, that they may treasure their ancient faith.
For unity among Christians, that the Cross may break down every dividing wall.
For those who suffer, that they may find in the Cross a source of living water.
For those whose hearts are troubled, that they may find Jesus the Way.
For our parish, that we may honour the Cross by lives of love and sacrifice.
pm.close: Lord God, from the Cross of your Son flows living water. Through the prayers of St Thomas the apostle, keep us faithful to the faith of our fathers and lead us by the Way of the Cross to your house. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A widow in Kuravilangad hung a Mar Thoma cross in her kitchen after her husband's death. “When I look at it,” she said, “I remember that the Cross ends in flowers. My sorrow will end in flowers too.”

quick: God calls us before we are born.
Jesus comes from above and speaks God's words.
God gives the Spirit without measure.
2026-12-19.action: Set up the crib at home with your family.
2026-12-19.question: Is Christ “above all” in my life?

family.explain: John the Baptist said Jesus is the greatest, because he comes from heaven. John was happy to be small so that Jesus could be big.
family.intention: We pray for people who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Jesus bigger in our family this Christmas?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come from above and are above all. As we gather, help us decrease so that you may increase in us. Amen.
share: God set Paul apart before he was born (Galatians 1:15). How do I experience God's call in my life?
John says the one from above is above all (John 3:31). Is Jesus truly first in my life?
Whom do I know who is far from Christ, and how can I pray for them?
pm.resp: He must increase; we must decrease.
interc: For the Church, that she may always point to Christ, like John the Baptist.
For those who persecute Christians, that like Saul they may be converted.
For those far from faith, that the Son may be revealed to them.
For our young people, that they may discover God's call before their birth.
For our families, that Jesus may be first in our homes.
pm.close: Lord God, you revealed your Son to Paul and made him an apostle. Reveal him to us and to all who seek, and give us the eternal life that comes from believing in him. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young engineer in Bengaluru who had mocked his Christian roommate for years was given a New Testament as a joke gift. He read John's Gospel in one night. Two years later he was baptised. He said: “I didn't find him. He found me.”

quick: The child of Bethlehem is the eternal Word.
The darkness cannot overcome his light.
Prayer prepares the heart to receive him.
2026-12-21.action: Read John 1:1–14 each day until Christmas.
2026-12-21.question: Where is the darkness in my life that Christ must enlighten?

family.explain: Before the world was made, Jesus was with God. He is the light that darkness can never put out.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel they live in darkness this Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “Let us light a candle tonight. Where do we need Jesus' light?”

pm.open: Eternal Word of the Father, light of the world, shine on us as we gather. Teach us to pray at all times and give us boldness to proclaim you. Amen.
share: Paul asks for boldness to proclaim the Gospel (Ephesians 6:19). Where do I lack courage to speak of Christ?
The light shines in the darkness (John 1:5). What darkness in my life needs his light?
How will I pray more in these last days before Christmas?
pm.resp: Christ our light, shine upon us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mystery of the Word made flesh with boldness.
For persecuted Christians, that they may be strengthened by prayer.
For priests and preachers, that they may speak with courage this Christmas.
For those in darkness, illness or despair, that Christ's light may reach them.
For our families, that we may pray together in these holy days.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, eternal Word, you came as light into our darkness. Keep us alert in prayer and bold in witness, and let your light shine through us this Christmas. Amen.

illus: An illustration

During a power cut in a Kottayam hostel, a student lit a single candle in the corridor. One by one, others came out with their own candles and lit them from it. Soon the corridor was full of light. One small light, shared, overcame the darkness.

quick: In the fullness of time God sent his Son, born of a woman.
Through him we are children and heirs.
Christmas is a choice: to receive him.
2026-12-22.action: Make one concrete space for Christ this Christmas.
2026-12-22.question: Have I truly received Christ, or only celebrated around him?

family.explain: Some people did not welcome Jesus. But to those who welcome him, he gives the gift of becoming God's children.
family.intention: We pray that our family may make room for Jesus this Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make room for Jesus, and for someone in need, at Christmas?”

pm.open: Abba, Father, in the fullness of time you sent your Son, born of a woman. As we gather, pour the Spirit of your Son into our hearts and make us your children. Amen.
share: God sent his Son born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). What does it mean to me that God became a real child?
His own people did not accept him (John 1:11). Where in my life is there ‘no room’ for him?
How will I receive him this Christmas?
pm.resp: Abba, Father, we are your children.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome Christ and make room for the poor.
For expectant mothers this Christmas, that they may be safe and joyful.
For those who reject Christ, that they may come to receive him.
For migrants, strangers and the homeless, that they may find welcome.
For our families, that we may live as children of God.
pm.close: Father, through your Son born of Mary you have made us your children. Make room in our hearts for him, and let us welcome him in every stranger this Christmas. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A family in Thodupuzha decided to leave one place empty at their Christmas table, with a lit candle, for “the stranger Jesus”. That year they invited a lonely migrant worker from Odisha who lived nearby. Their children still remember it as their best Christmas.

quick: Isaiah's names for the Child meet our deepest needs.
Finish the fast well and make peace.
Prepare a place for the Child.
2026-12-23.action: Reconcile with someone before Christmas Eve.
2026-12-23.question: Which of Christ's names do I need most this Christmas?

family.explain: Isaiah gave baby Jesus four beautiful names. Each name tells us how Jesus helps us.
family.intention: We pray for peace in families that are quarrelling this Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of Jesus' four names do we need most this year?”

pm.open: Come, Lord Jesus, Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. As we gather on the eve of your coming, prepare our hearts to welcome you. Amen.
share: Which of the four names of the Child (Isaiah 9:6) speaks most to my situation now?
With whom do I need to make peace before Christmas?
How will I finish this Nombu well?
pm.resp: Come, Prince of Peace.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a sign of the Prince of Peace in the world.
For those facing difficult decisions, that the Wonderful Counsellor may guide them.
For the weak and the addicted, that the Mighty God may strengthen them.
For the lonely, that the Everlasting Father may comfort them.
For families and nations in conflict, that the Prince of Peace may reconcile them.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son comes as Counsellor, Mighty God, Father and Prince of Peace. Make us ready to receive him in these last days of waiting. Amen.

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in Muvattupuzha had not spoken for six years over a land boundary. Two days before Christmas, the younger brother walked over with a plum cake. Neither said much. But at the midnight Qurbana they stood side by side. The Prince of Peace had come early.

quick: God chooses the small: little Bethlehem.
Bethlehem means “house of bread”.
Make room for silent adoration tonight.
2026-12-24.action: Call someone who will be alone this Christmas.
2026-12-24.question: Will there be silence for Jesus in my Christmas Eve?

family.explain: God chose little Bethlehem for Jesus to be born. Bethlehem means ‘house of bread’. Jesus came to feed us with his love.
family.intention: We pray for all families gathering tonight, and for those who are alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift will each of us give to baby Jesus tonight?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, tonight you come to Bethlehem, the house of bread. As we wait in joy, quiet our hearts and prepare us to adore you. Amen.
share: God chose little Bethlehem (Micah 5:2). Where do I see God choosing the small in my life?
What noise must I silence tonight to adore the Child?
What gift will I bring to the manger?
pm.resp: Come, Lord Jesus, come.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may welcome Christ with joy tonight.
For families gathering for Christmas, that they may be united in love.
For those who are alone, sick or grieving tonight.
For the poor and homeless, who share the poverty of the stable.
For peace in the Holy Land and in all places of war.
pm.close: Lord God, you chose little Bethlehem for the birth of your Son. Make our hearts a humble stable where he may be born tonight, and fill our homes with his peace. Amen.

illus: An illustration

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this second Sunday of Annunciation we enter the house of Nazareth. The angel Gabriel greets a young woman: “Greetings, favoured one! The Lord is with you.” He tells her she will bear a son, the Son of the Most High, whose kingdom will have no end.

Mary is not a passive listener. She asks, “How can this be?” The angel explains: the Holy Spirit will come upon you. And then Mary says the most important word ever spoken by a human being: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” With that yes, God became man.

The first reading tells a strange story. Balaam, a famous prophet, rides along a road and cannot see the angel blocking his path. His donkey sees the angel; the prophet does not. Only when God opens his eyes does Balaam understand. How often we are like Balaam: busy, blind, going our own way, while God stands in front of us.

Mary is the opposite of Balaam. She sees, she listens, she says yes. Isaiah promised: “I will pour my spirit upon your descendants.” At Nazareth that promise came true. And the same Spirit comes upon the bread and wine at every Qurbana and upon us.

This week, let us ask God to open our eyes, and let us learn Mary's word: “Let it be with me according to your word.” Let us pray the Angelus each day and say yes to God in one concrete thing. Then Christ will be born again in us. Amen.
kids: Children, an angel came to a young girl named Mary and told her some amazing news: she would be the mother of Jesus, God's Son!
Mary could have said no. But she said, “Yes! I am God's servant.” Because Mary said yes, Jesus came into the world.
Let's say yes to God like Mary. Say together: “Yes, Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate a birth. After long years of waiting, Elizabeth gives birth to a son, and her neighbours rejoice with her because the Lord has shown his great mercy.

The Old Testament readings show us that this is not the first time. Abraham, sitting at his tent in the heat of the day, welcomes three visitors and hears that Sarah will have a son. The barren wife of Manoah hears that she will bear Samson, consecrated to God. God's plan of salvation moves forward through children born by his grace.

At the naming, the relatives want to call the child Zechariah. Elizabeth says, “No; he is to be called John.” And Zechariah, who could not speak for nine months, writes: “His name is John.” Immediately his tongue is freed and he praises God. When we finally obey God's word, we too begin to praise.

“John” means “God has been gracious.” That is the message of this whole season. Christmas is not first our achievement; it is God's grace. And the people ask: “What then will this child become?” For the hand of the Lord was with him.

Every child in our families is such a promise. Let us bless our children, pray for them, and help them discover the hand of the Lord upon them. And let us, like Zechariah, open our mouths in praise, for God has been gracious to us. Amen.
kids: Children, when a baby is born, everyone is happy, right? When John the Baptist was born, all the neighbours came to celebrate!
His dad Zechariah couldn't talk for nine months. But when he wrote “His name is John”, suddenly he could talk again, and he praised God!
Your name is special too, and God has a plan for you. Say together: “Thank you, God, for my name and my life!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday before Christmas the Church turns our eyes to St Joseph. Mary is expecting a child, and Joseph knows it is not his. He is a righteous man, and he does not want to shame her, so he decides to dismiss her quietly.

Then God speaks to him in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus.” And the Gospel says simply: Joseph woke up and did as the angel commanded. Not a word of complaint. Not a single word at all.

The Old Testament gives us two more pictures of God working in families. Rebekah is asked, “Will you go with this man?” and she says, “I will.” Hannah, childless and mocked, pours out her soul before the Lord, and God gives her Samuel. God's will is found in prayer and accepted with trust.

St Paul says: “Understand what the will of the Lord is.” Joseph did not understand everything. But he understood enough to obey. That is the faith Christmas asks of us: not to have all the answers, but to do what God asks.

Fathers, look at Joseph: he protects, he provides, he obeys, he loves in silence. Families, look at Joseph: he takes Mary and Jesus into his home. This Christmas, let us not be afraid to take Jesus and Mary into our homes. St Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know who took care of baby Jesus? His mother Mary and St Joseph!
An angel told Joseph in a dream: “Don't be afraid! Take care of Mary and the baby.” Joseph woke up and did it right away.
Let's be like St Joseph: quick to obey and kind to our family. Say together: “St Joseph, help me obey God!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and holy Christmas to all of you! Tonight the angel speaks to us as he spoke to the shepherds: “Do not be afraid; I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people: to you is born this day a Saviour, who is the Messiah, the Lord.”

This is the heart of our faith. The eternal Son of God, through whom all things were made, has become a man. He did not come as a king in a palace, but as a baby in a manger, because there was no room for him in the inn. Isaiah had promised: “A child has been born for us, a son given to us… Prince of Peace.” Micah had promised that he would come from little Bethlehem. Tonight the promises are fulfilled.

Who heard the news first? Not the powerful in Rome or Jerusalem, but poor shepherds in the fields at night. God comes first to the little, the forgotten, those working through the night. And the sign is so humble: a child wrapped in cloths, lying in a manger. If we look for God in power and noise, we will miss him. He is found in humility.

Bethlehem means “house of bread”, and the manger is a feeding place. Our Syriac Fathers loved this: the Bread of Life was laid where food is placed. In a few moments that same Lord will be on our altar, and we will receive him. That is our Christmas: Christ born in us.

So let us do what the shepherds did: go with haste, adore him, and then go back glorifying God and telling others. And let us do what Mary did: treasure these things in our hearts. May the Prince of Peace bring peace to your homes, to our country and to the whole world. A blessed Christmas to you all! Amen.
kids: Children, Happy Christmas! Today we celebrate Jesus' birthday!
Jesus is God's Son, but he was born as a tiny baby in Bethlehem. There was no room in the hotel, so his mother Mary laid him in a manger, where animals eat!
Angels sang, “Glory to God!” and shepherds came running to see him. Let's sing too! Say together: “Happy birthday, Jesus! I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a joyful and blessed Christmas to all of you! Tonight let us go in spirit to a small town in Judea. Its name was Bethlehem. In Hebrew, Bethlehem means house of bread. It was there, and nowhere else, that God chose to be born.

The prophet Micah had foretold it: from you, Bethlehem, small among the clans of Judah, shall come forth one who is to rule in Israel (Micah 5:2). God plans with care. The One who would say I am the bread of life (John 6:35) was born in the house of bread.

And where did Mary lay Him? In a manger (Luke 2:7). We have made the crib beautiful with lights and decorations, but a manger was a feeding trough, the place where animals came to eat. The prophet Isaiah had said that the ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's crib, but Israel does not understand (Isaiah 1:3). The Son of God was placed where food is placed. From His first night on earth He was saying: I have come to be your food.

That is why Christmas leads us to the altar. In a few moments, on this altar, the same Christ born in Bethlehem will become present under the appearance of bread. The shepherds knelt at the manger; we kneel before the Holy Qurbana. They saw a child; we see bread. In both cases faith sees God hidden in humility. Receive Him tonight with the faith of the shepherds.

And the shepherds did not keep the good news to themselves. They told everyone what they had heard (Luke 2:17). Bread is meant to be shared. This Christmas, share your bread with someone who is hungry, lonely or forgotten: a meal, a visit, a phone call. Then Christmas will not end tonight. It will continue in every house where Christ, the Bread of Life, is received and shared.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Incarnation, true God and true man
intro: Christmas is not only a sweet story. It is the heart of our faith: God became man.

sub: The eternal Son took a human nature (John 1:14).
Not a phantom, not a half-god.
For us and for our salvation (Nicene Creed).
points.apply: Bow deeply at the words of the Creed: and became man.

sub: One divine Person, two natures (CCC 464–469).
Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus, Chalcedon.
Mary is truly Mother of God, Theotokos (CCC 495).
points.apply: Call Mary Mother of God with faith in the Hail Mary.

sub: To reconcile us with God (CCC 457).
To show us God's love (CCC 458).
To be our model of holiness and to make us sharers in the divine nature (CCC 459–460).
points.apply: Thank God that He came to make you His child.

concl: The Incarnation is the greatest proof of God's love.
God became man so that we might share His divine life.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will bow at the words of the Creed and thank God for becoming man.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed Christmas to you all! We have heard the familiar story again: the journey, the manger, the shepherds. But behind the story is the most astonishing truth ever proclaimed: God became man. Tonight let us look at this mystery as the Church teaches it.

St John writes: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; and the Word became flesh and lived among us (John 1:1, 14). The Child in the manger is not a good man whom God later adopted, nor a god who only seemed human. He is the eternal Son of God who took to Himself a full human nature, body and soul, in the womb of the Virgin Mary. That is why, in the Creed, at the words and became man, we bow; on Christmas day, we kneel.

The early Church had to defend this truth against many errors. The Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus and Chalcedon taught that Jesus Christ is one divine Person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion and without separation (CCC 464–469). Because the Child is God, the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God (CCC 495). This is not an exaggeration about Mary; it is a protection of the truth about Jesus.

Why did God become man? The Catechism gives four reasons. To save us by reconciling us with God. So that we might know God's love. To be our model of holiness. And to make us partakers of the divine nature (CCC 457–460; 2 Peter 1:4). The Fathers of the Church summed it up: the Son of God became a son of man so that we might become children of God.

So Christmas is not only for children; it is the foundation of our whole faith. At this Holy Qurbana the same Word made flesh comes to us. Let us receive Him with wonder, and let His love, so humble and so close, change the way we live.

opts.a: Peace on earth: the angels' song and our reconciliation
intro: On the night of the Nativity the sky over Bethlehem was filled with an army of angels singing glory to God and peace on earth (Luke 2:13–14). Two thousand years later the world still longs for that peace: in the Holy Land where Christ was born, in every land torn by war or communal conflict, and in many of our own homes.
Tonight the Prince of Peace is born. He does not bring peace by force, but by coming close to us, small and defenceless.

sub: Peace is first a gift from God, not an agreement among people.
It comes through a Child: the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6).
Christ is our peace; he breaks down the walls of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).
points.apply: Ask the Child tonight for the gift of an inner peace that does not depend on circumstances.

sub: Families divided over property, words or old hurts.
Brothers who have not spoken for years.
Couples who live under one roof but far apart.
points.apply: Before the Christmas meal is over, take one step towards someone you are not at peace with.

points.h: Makers of peace in the world
sub: Pray for peace in the Holy Land and wherever there is war.
Refuse hatred and division on social media.
Blessed are the peacemakers (Matthew 5:9).
points.apply: Pray each day of the Christmas season for one country at war.

concl: The angels sang peace on earth among those whom God favours. God's favour rests on all who receive his Son. At this Holy Qurbana, let us exchange the sign of peace with sincerity, and carry it home.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will make peace with one person, and pray daily for one nation at war.
homily: Dear friends, on the night of the Nativity the shepherds heard the angels sing: glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favours (Luke 2:14). Glory to God and peace on earth go together. When God is given his glory, peace follows.

Isaiah had called the Child the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6). Strange prince: born in a stable, laid in a manger, threatened by a king. Yet he brings what no army can bring. St Paul says: he is our peace; in his flesh he has broken down the dividing wall of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).

The world longs for peace. Tonight we pray for the land where Jesus was born, for all places torn by war, and for our own country wherever communities are divided. Christmas is not a holiday from the world's pain; it is God entering it.

But peace begins closer. In many families tonight there is an empty chair, not because of death, but because of a quarrel. Brothers who do not speak, sisters divided over property, a son estranged from his father. The Child in the manger asks: will you let me bring peace into your home?

Jacob, after twenty years of fear, ran to meet his brother Esau, and Esau embraced him (Genesis 33:4). Jesus taught: if your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Christmas is the best time to take that first step: a phone call, a visit, a slice of cake carried across the road.

At this Holy Qurbana, when we offer one another the sign of peace, let it be real. And let us go home as peacemakers, for blessed are the peacemakers; they will be called children of God (Matthew 5:9). A blessed and peaceful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: Good news to the shepherds: Christ comes to the poor and the margins
intro: The first to hear the news of Christmas were not kings or priests, but shepherds: poor, rough, often despised, working through the night. God chose them as the first witnesses of his Son (Luke 2:8–12).
Christmas is good news for all who live at the edges: migrant workers, night-shift nurses, fishermen, farmers, the homeless and the forgotten.

sub: Shepherds were poor and considered unclean.
Yet David, the shepherd boy, became king.
The Good Shepherd is announced first to shepherds.
points.apply: Remember that God's first messengers went to those the world overlooks.

sub: The sign was not power, but a baby in a manger.
God meets us in poverty and simplicity.
The shepherds recognised him because he was like them.
points.apply: Look for Christ this Christmas in a poor person near you.

points.h: They went with haste and told others
sub: The shepherds did not keep the news to themselves.
They returned glorifying and praising God.
The poor became the first evangelisers.
points.apply: Share the joy of Christmas with someone who has no one to celebrate with.

concl: The Child who came first to shepherds comes now to us at this Holy Qurbana. Let us welcome him with simple hearts, and go out like the shepherds to tell others what we have seen.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will share a meal or a gift with a migrant worker, a night worker or a poor family.
homily: Dear friends, on that first Christmas night, while Bethlehem slept, shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks in the fields. To them, not to the powerful in Jerusalem or Rome, an angel appeared and said: do not be afraid; I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people (Luke 2:10).

Shepherds in those days were poor and often looked down upon. Their work kept them away from the Temple and from respectable company. Yet God chose them. The prophet Ezekiel had promised that God himself would shepherd his people, seek the lost and bind up the injured (Ezekiel 34:11–16). The Good Shepherd announces himself first to shepherds.

The sign they were given was not a palace or a crown, but a child wrapped in bands of cloth and lying in a manger (Luke 2:12). The poor recognised him because he was poor like them. God did not come to the world from above, but from below.

Think of the shepherds of our time: the migrant worker from another state who builds our houses, the nurse on night duty in a hospital abroad, the fisherman at sea on Christmas night, the security guard at the gate, the family in a rented room. Christmas is first their feast.

The shepherds went with haste, found Mary and Joseph and the child, and then made known what had been told them. They returned glorifying and praising God (Luke 2:16–20). The poor became the first evangelists. They had nothing to give but their joy, and it was enough.

At this Holy Qurbana, Christ comes to us as he came to the shepherds: simply, humbly. Let us receive him, and then, like them, go out with haste: to share our Christmas food, to visit someone alone, to bring good news to the margins. A joyful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: A Christmas homily for families and children
intro: This homily is written for a congregation with many children and families. It uses simple words and three images the children can remember: the star, the crib and the gift.
Christmas is a family feast because God chose to be born into a family.

points.h: The star: God shows the way
sub: The star led the wise men to Jesus.
Our Christmas stars remind us: Jesus is the light.
Parents are stars for their children, showing the way to God.
points.apply: Let each family pray together tonight under the Christmas star.

sub: The great God became a little baby.
He chose a poor family and a simple place.
He wants a place in our homes and hearts.
points.apply: Let the children place the Child in the home crib with a prayer.

sub: At Christmas we give gifts because God gave us Jesus.
The best gift is love: time, kindness, forgiveness.
Jesus gives himself again at the Holy Qurbana.
points.apply: Let each person give one gift of love tomorrow that costs no money.

concl: The star shows the way, the crib shows God's humility, and the gift shows his love. May every family leave this Holy Qurbana with the Child in their hearts.
opts.resolve: Our family will pray together before the crib every evening until the end of the Christmas season.
homily: Dear children and dear families, a very happy Christmas to you! Tonight I want to talk about three things you can see around you: the star, the crib and the gift.

First, the star. Look at the stars shining in our homes and in the church. Long ago a star led the wise men to the place where Jesus was (Matthew 2:9–10). Our stars remind us that Jesus is the light of the world. And, dear parents, you are stars for your children: by your prayer and your example, you show them the way to Jesus.

Second, the crib. Look at the crib: Mary, Joseph, the shepherds, the animals, and the little baby. Isn't it amazing? The great God, who made the sun and the stars and the sea, became a tiny baby. He did not choose a palace; he was laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn (Luke 2:7). Children, Jesus wants a place in your home and in your heart. Will you make room for him?

Third, the gift. Why do we give gifts at Christmas? Because God gave us the best gift: his own Son. God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:16). So our gifts are a little copy of God's love. But the best gifts do not come from a shop: a hug, helping at home, saying sorry, sharing with a poor child.
And there is one more gift. At this Holy Qurbana, Jesus gives himself to us again. The baby of Bethlehem comes to us in Holy Communion. Bethlehem means house of bread, and Jesus is the Bread of Life.

So when you go home tonight, look at the star and say: Jesus, you are my light. Look at the crib and say: Jesus, come into my heart. And give one gift of love tomorrow. A happy and holy Christmas to every family. Amen.
Dear brothers and sisters, two days after Christmas we look at the family in which Jesus grew up: the Holy Family of Nazareth.

It was not a comfortable family. Soon after Jesus was born, the angel told Joseph: “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt.” They became refugees in a foreign land. Later they came back and lived quietly in Nazareth, a small village, working with their hands.

The readings show God's plan for the family. In the beginning God created man and woman in his image and blessed them. Sirach tells children to honour their parents and care for them in old age. St Paul describes a home led by Christ: husbands and wives who love and respect one another, children who obey, parents who do not discourage their children.

The Holy Family was holy not because it had no problems, but because it faced its problems with God. Joseph protected, Mary pondered, Jesus obeyed and grew in wisdom. Many of our families today are stretched: a parent working abroad, a sick member, money worries, quarrels. The Holy Family knows that road.

So today let us bring our families to Jesus, Mary and Joseph. Let us pray together at home, honour our parents, care for our elders, and forgive one another. Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our families. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus had a family too: his mother Mary and St Joseph!
When Jesus was a baby, a bad king wanted to hurt him. So Joseph took Mary and Jesus far away to Egypt to keep them safe. Later they came home to Nazareth.
Our family is special too. Let's help at home and pray together. Say together: “Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless my family!”

intro: St Joseph never speaks a single word in the Gospels, yet he protects the Holy Family at every danger.

sub: Four dreams, four obediences (Matthew 1:20; 2:13, 19, 22).
He rose and did as he was told.
Listening to God in silence.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence with God each day.

sub: Flight to Egypt by night (Matthew 2:13–15).
Work and sacrifice for wife and child.
Fathers as guardians of the home.
points.apply: Fathers: bless your children tonight.

sub: Just: faithful to God's law with mercy (Matthew 1:19).
He did not expose Mary to shame.
Justice and tenderness together.
points.apply: Correct with gentleness, never with humiliation.

concl: Joseph shows how to guard a family: with silence, obedience, work and tenderness.
Every family can ask St Joseph to be its protector.
opts.resolve: Our family will consecrate itself to the protection of St Joseph this week.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this feast of the Holy Family let us look at the one member who never says a word in the Gospels: St Joseph. Mary speaks, Jesus speaks, angels speak, but Joseph only listens and acts.

Four times an angel speaks to Joseph in a dream, and four times he obeys at once: to take Mary as his wife, to flee to Egypt, to return to the land of Israel, and to settle in Nazareth (Matthew 1:20; 2:13, 19, 22). Each time the Gospel says simply that Joseph got up and did as he was told. In a world full of noise, Joseph teaches us to listen to God in silence and to act without delay.

Joseph was a protector. When Herod sought to kill the child, Joseph took the child and his mother by night and fled to Egypt (Matthew 2:14). Think of that journey: a refugee family, poor, in a foreign land, with a little baby. Joseph worked with his hands to feed them. Today many fathers work far from home, in the Gulf or abroad, to support their families. Joseph understands them.

The Gospel calls Joseph a just man (Matthew 1:19). When he discovered that Mary was with child, he did not want to expose her to public disgrace. His justice was full of mercy. In our families too, justice and tenderness must go together: correction without humiliation, firmness without harshness, forgiveness without weakness.

Fathers, look at Joseph: protect your families, work honestly, pray, bless your children. Mothers, look at Mary. Children, look at Jesus, who was obedient to His parents. And let every family here entrust itself to St Joseph, guardian of the Redeemer. May he who guarded the Holy Family guard ours too.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Christian family as domestic church
intro: The Church calls the family a domestic church. What does that mean in practice?

sub: Lumen Gentium 11: the family as domestic church.
Parents as first teachers of the faith (CCC 1656).
Prayer, Word, sacraments at the centre.
points.apply: Begin or renew daily family prayer.

sub: Honour your father and mother (CCC 2214–2220).
Parents' duty to educate in faith and virtue (CCC 2221–2226).
Care for elderly parents.
points.apply: Visit or call an elderly relative this week.

sub: Migration, screens, addiction, broken marriages.
The Holy Family also faced danger and exile.
The parish as family of families.
points.apply: Eat at least one meal a day together without phones.

concl: The family is where faith is first received, prayed and lived.
Nazareth is a school for every family.
opts.resolve: Our family will pray together every evening and share one meal a day without phones.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Second Vatican Council gave the Christian family a beautiful name: the domestic church (Lumen Gentium 11). On the feast of the Holy Family, let us see what this means in practice.

A church is a place where God is worshipped, His Word is heard and love is lived. The home is meant to be exactly that. Parents are the first heralds of the faith for their children (CCC 1656). Long before catechism class, children learn from their parents how to make the sign of the cross, how to fold their hands, how to forgive. Moses told the Israelites to speak of God's words at home and on the road, when lying down and when rising (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The Fourth Commandment teaches children to honour their father and mother, with respect, gratitude, obedience while they are young, and care for them when they are old (CCC 2214–2220; Sirach 3:1–14). It also gives parents duties: to educate their children in faith, in prayer and in virtue, to respect their vocation, and to give the example of a good life (CCC 2221–2226). St Paul writes: fathers, do not provoke your children, or they may lose heart (Colossians 3:21).

Families today are under great pressure: work far from home, financial stress, screens that keep everyone apart in the same room, addiction, broken marriages. The Holy Family also knew danger, poverty and exile. They survived because God was at the centre. Let our families do the same: pray together every evening, even briefly; eat at least one meal a day together without phones; come to the Holy Qurbana together on Sunday; forgive before sleeping.

And let the parish be a family of families, supporting those who are struggling, single parents, widows, the elderly living alone. May Jesus, Mary and Joseph bless every family in this parish, and make our homes true domestic churches.

Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Many people confuse this feast with the virginal conception of Jesus. Today's feast is about Mary herself: from the first moment of her life in her mother's womb, God preserved her from original sin.

Why? Because God was preparing a home for his Son. The book of Sirach describes Wisdom looking for a place to pitch its tent. Isaiah promised a sign: the young woman will bear a son, Immanuel. When the Son of God came, he needed a mother, and God prepared her with a singular grace.

The Church teaches that Mary was preserved from sin in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. So Mary too was saved by her Son, but in a wonderful way: not lifted out of the mud, but kept from falling into it. That is why the angel called her “full of grace”.

And Mary herself tells us the secret of her greatness in the Magnificat: “He has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant… the Mighty One has done great things for me.” Not pride, but gratitude. Everything is God's mercy.

What God did in Mary at the beginning, he wants to do in us at the end: to make us holy and blameless before him in love. So in this season, let us prepare a clean heart for Jesus by a good confession. Holy Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to you. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary was kept free from every sin by God from the very first moment of her life. Ask Mary to help you keep your heart clean and full of love for Jesus!

opts.a: Mary, the new Eve and the Ark of the Covenant
intro: The Fathers of the Church loved to read the Old Testament with Mary in mind. Two images help us understand this feast: the new Eve and the Ark.

sub: Eve listened to the serpent; Mary listened to the angel.
Eve's disobedience brought death; Mary's obedience opened the way to life.
St Irenaeus: the knot of Eve was untied by Mary.
points.apply: When tempted, say Mary's words: let it be done according to your word.

sub: The Ark held the tablets, the manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4).
Mary carried the Word, the Bread of Life, the eternal Priest.
The Ark was made pure; Mary was preserved from all stain.
points.apply: Receive Christ in the Holy Qurbana with a clean heart, like Mary.

sub: God prepared a pure dwelling for His Son.
Mary was redeemed in a more exalted way.
What God did for her, He wants to begin in us.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Christmas.

concl: Mary Immaculate shows us what grace can do and what we are called to be.
The feast in Advent prepares a clean dwelling for Christ in us.
opts.resolve: Before Christmas I will make a good confession to prepare a clean dwelling for Christ.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the early Christians did not have the dogma of the Immaculate Conception in its later words, but they had a deep intuition about Mary, drawn from the Scriptures. Let us look at two images that the Fathers loved: Mary as the new Eve, and Mary as the Ark of the Covenant.

In the garden, Eve listened to the serpent and believed his lie. Through her disobedience, sin and death entered the world. But God promised that the offspring of a woman would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). In Nazareth another woman listened, not to a serpent but to an angel, and said: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). St Irenaeus wrote that the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience. Where Eve said no, Mary said yes.

The second image is the Ark of the Covenant. God commanded Moses to make it of acacia wood, covered with pure gold inside and out (Exodus 25:10–11). Inside were the tablets of the law, a jar of manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4). When the Ark entered a house, it brought blessing; David danced before it. Mary carried in her womb the Word of God, the true Bread from heaven and the eternal High Priest. When she entered Elizabeth's house, the child leaped for joy (Luke 1:41). If the Ark had to be pure gold, how much more the living Ark of the Son of God.

This is what the Church proclaims today: that from the first moment of her conception Mary was preserved from every stain of original sin, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. She too was saved by her Son, but in a more exalted way: preserved rather than cleansed.

And what God did perfectly for Mary, He wants to begin in us. In Baptism we were washed; in confession we are cleansed again; in the Holy Qurbana we receive Christ as Mary did. This Advent, let us prepare a clean dwelling for Him. Make a good confession before Christmas, and ask Mary Immaculate to teach you to say yes.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the dogma of the Immaculate Conception
intro: Many people confuse this feast with the virginal conception of Jesus. Let us be clear about what the Church teaches and why.

sub: Defined by Pope Pius IX in 1854 (Ineffabilis Deus).
Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception (CCC 491).
By a singular grace, in view of the merits of Christ.
points.apply: Learn the difference between the Immaculate Conception and the Virgin Birth.

sub: The angel's greeting: kecharitomene, highly favoured, filled with grace (Luke 1:28).
Mary was redeemed by her Son (CCC 492).
She remained free of personal sin all her life (CCC 493).
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly, attentive to the words full of grace.

points.h: Lourdes and the faith of the people
sub: 1858: I am the Immaculate Conception.
Eastern tradition: Mary the All-Holy, Panagia (CCC 493).
Our own Churches' devotion to Mary.
points.apply: Honour Mary this Advent with the Rosary.

concl: The dogma honours Christ, whose grace made Mary all-holy.
Mary Immaculate is the model and mother of the Church.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray the Rosary and ask Mary to make my heart pure.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, many Catholics think that today's feast is about the conception of Jesus in Mary's womb. It is not. That we celebrate on 25 March, the Annunciation. Today we celebrate the conception of Mary herself in the womb of her mother, whom tradition names Anne.

On 8 December 1854, Pope Pius IX solemnly defined that the most Blessed Virgin Mary, from the first moment of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God, and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ the Saviour of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin (CCC 491). Every word matters. Singular grace: it was God's gift, not Mary's achievement. In view of the merits of Jesus Christ: Mary too was saved by her Son.

Where is this in the Bible? The angel greets Mary as full of grace (Luke 1:28). The Greek word means one who has been, and remains, filled with God's favour. The Church understood that the woman chosen to be the Mother of God was prepared by grace from the beginning. The Catechism says that Mary was redeemed from the moment of her conception, and that by God's grace she remained free of every personal sin her whole life long (CCC 492–493). The Eastern Fathers call her Panagia, the All-Holy.

Four years after the definition, in 1858, Our Lady appeared to a poor girl, Bernadette, at Lourdes. When Bernadette asked her name, she answered: I am the Immaculate Conception. Bernadette did not understand the words, but the parish priest did. Heaven confirmed what the Church had taught.

Why does this matter? Because it shows what God's grace can do. Mary is not a goddess; she is a creature, entirely filled with grace. She shows what the Church is called to become: holy and without blemish (Ephesians 5:27). So let us honour her this Advent with the Rosary, and ask her to help us prepare for her Son at this Holy Qurbana and at Christmas.

Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated the birth of Christ; today we celebrate the death of St Stephen, the first martyr. It seems strange to move from the crib to the stones so quickly. But the Church wants us to understand: the Child born in Bethlehem calls for a faith that is ready to give everything.
Stephen was full of grace and power, doing great wonders and signs among the people (Acts 6:8). His enemies could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke. So they stoned him.

As he was dying, Stephen saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:56). Then he prayed two prayers that echo Jesus on the Cross: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit; and, Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:59–60).

In the Gospel Jesus warns: I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves; be wise as serpents and innocent as doves. You will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:16, 22).

Stephen's greatest miracle was not his signs; it was his forgiveness. And a young man named Saul, guarding the coats of those who stoned him, would later become St Paul. Stephen's forgiveness bore fruit.

Christians are persecuted in many places today, including parts of India. Let us pray for them. And let us ask for Stephen's spirit in our ordinary lives: to forgive those who hurt us, even while the hurt is still fresh. That is the true gift of Christmas. Amen.
kids: Children, St Stephen loved Jesus so much that he forgave the people who hurt him. Can you forgive someone today?

homily: Dear friends, the joy of Christmas is followed by tears. Herod, furious at being tricked by the Magi, killed all the children in and around Bethlehem who were two years old or under (Matthew 2:16). Matthew hears in the mothers' cry the voice of Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be consoled, because they are no more (Matthew 2:18; Jeremiah 31:15).

The first reading takes us back to the beginning: Cain kills his brother Abel (Genesis 4:8). From the first family, innocent blood has cried to God. The Holy Innocents join this long line, and they are the first to die in the place of Christ.

Why does God allow this? We do not have a full answer. But Christmas tells us that God did not stay distant from suffering. He came into a world where children are killed, and he himself would be killed. He is with the innocent who suffer.

The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of those who suffered for their faith: they were stoned, sawn in two, killed by the sword; of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:37–38). The Holy Innocents could not speak, but their lives witnessed to Christ.
